ITQAN:v1p89#2/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p89#2/r3.speaker: محمد بن كعب القرظي
ITQAN:v1p89#2/r3.claim: In a conversation with Said al-Maqburi, Muhammad ibn Kab says a verse may be revealed about one person and then apply generally.
ITQAN:v1p89#2/r3.anchor: إن الآية تنزل في الرجل ثم تكون عامة بعد

MAJAZ:v1p70/r8.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p70/r8.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p70/r8.claim: Aladd al-khiṣām means intensely contentious; al-ibil and al-add can also describe a wicked person, and ludd is the plural of ladīd.
MAJAZ:v1p70/r8.anchor: «ألد الخصام» (204) : شديد الخصومة، ويقال للفاجر: أبل وألد، ويقال:

MAJAZ:v1p70/r9.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p70/r9.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p70/r9.claim: Al-Musayyib ibn ʿAlas’s verse calls the obstinate person al-ibil al-muṣammam, supporting the usage of ludd.
MAJAZ:v1p70/r9.anchor: ألا تتقون الله يا آل عامر ... وهل يتقى الله الإبل المصمم

STUDYQURAN:2:204/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:204/r1.speaker: IK, R, Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:2:204/r1.claim: Most cited commentators prefer to read 2:204–7 as universal teaching on hypocrisy, despite reports of specific incidents.
STUDYQURAN:2:204/r1.anchor: most prefer to see these verses as universal teachings on the nature of hypocrisy (IK, R, Ṭ)

STUDYQURAN:2:204/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:204/r2.speaker: some commentators
STUDYQURAN:2:204/r2.claim: Some commentators identify Akhnas ibn Shurayq al-Thaqafī as a hypocrite who feigned interest in Islam and claimed God knew his heart.
STUDYQURAN:2:204/r2.anchor: a certain Akhnas ibn Shurayq al-Thaqafī, who feigned interest in embracing Islam and even went so far as to say

STUDYQURAN:2:204/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:204/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:2:204/r3.claim: The verb translated impresses can mean please, evoke wonder, cause marvel, or delight.
STUDYQURAN:2:204/r3.anchor: rendered impresses can also mean “to please,” “to evoke wonder,” “to cause

STUDYQURAN:2:204/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:204/r4.speaker: Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:2:204/r4.claim: Fiercest of adversaries may also mean most crooked in disputation.

STUDYQURAN:2:204/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:204/r5.speaker: Th
STUDYQURAN:2:204/r5.claim: Another reported occasion is that Makkans feigned interest in Islam, requested learned teachers, then ambushed and killed the Prophet’s delegation near Makkah.
STUDYQURAN:2:204/r5.anchor: some Makkans pretended to want to learn about Islam and asked the Prophet to send a delegation of learned men to teach them

TAB-FULL:v3p572/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p572/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v3p572/r1.claim: The verse describes hypocrites whose public speech pleases Muhammad while they call God to witness about their hearts; their disputation is false and crooked.
TAB-FULL:v3p572/r1.anchor: الخصام، جدل بالباطل. ثم اختلف أهل التأويل

TAB-FULL:v3p572/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p572/r2.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v3p572/r2.claim: Al-Suddī says 2:204 concerns al-Akhnas b. Shurayq, who professed Islam and swore sincerity to the Prophet, then burned Muslim crops and killed their donkeys, prompting 2:205.
TAB-FULL:v3p572/r2.anchor: عن السدي " {ومن الناس من يعجبك قوله في الحياة الدنيا ويشهد الله على ما في قلبه

TAB-FULL:v3p572/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p572/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v3p572/r3.claim: Al-Ṭabarī glosses al-add al-khiṣām as crooked contention and associates the description of al-Akhnas with 104:1 and 68:10–13.
TAB-FULL:v3p572/r3.anchor: وأما ألد الخصام: فأعوج الخصام، وفيه نزل: {ويل لكل همزة لمزة} [الهمزة: 1] ونزلت فيه

TAB-FULL:v3p572/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p572/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v3p572/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports that hypocrites mocked the Muslims killed at al-Rajīʿ as having died pointlessly; the verses contrast their hypocrisy and corruption with the martyrs’ reward and those who give themselves for God.
TAB-FULL:v3p572/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قال " لما أصيبت هذه السرية أصحاب خبيب بالرجيع بين مكة، والمدينة، فقال رجال من المنافقين

TAB-FULL:v3p572/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p572/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v3p572/r5.claim: A second transmission of Ibn ʿAbbās’s al-Rajīʿ account names ʿĀṣim and Marthad among the expedition and says the report otherwise matches the preceding version.
TAB-FULL:v3p572/r5.anchor: عن عكرمة مولى ابن عباس أو عن سعيد بن جبير، عن ابن عباس، قال: «لما أصيبت السرية التي كان فيها عاصم، ومرثد، بالرجيع

TAB-FULL:v3p572/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p572/r6.speaker: آخرون
TAB-FULL:v3p572/r6.claim: Other interpreters take the description generally of all hypocrites, whose inward state differs from their outward profession.
TAB-FULL:v3p572/r6.anchor: وقال آخرون: بل نزل ذلك في قوم من أهل النفاق

TAB-FULL:v3p576/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p576/r1.speaker: سعيد المقبري
TAB-FULL:v3p576/r1.claim: Saʿīd al-Maqburī quotes a scripture describing people with honey-sweet tongues, bitter hearts, and soft outward manners who pursue worldly gain through religion; God threatens a trial that will bewilder the wise.
TAB-FULL:v3p576/r1.anchor: سمعت سعيدا المقبري يذاكر محمد بن كعب، فقال سعيد

TAB-FULL:v3p576/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p576/r2.speaker: محمد بن كعب
TAB-FULL:v3p576/r2.claim: Muḥammad b. Kaʿb identifies that description in Qurʾān 2:204–205 and says a verse first revealed about one man can afterward apply generally.
TAB-FULL:v3p576/r2.anchor: فقال محمد بن كعب: «إن الآية تنزل في الرجل ثم تكون عامة بعد»

TAB-FULL:v3p576/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p576/r3.speaker: نوف
TAB-FULL:v3p576/r3.claim: Nawf says he found a description of deceptive people in revealed scripture; al-Qurazī says reflection on the Qurʾān identifies them as hypocrites and points to 2:204 and 22:11.
TAB-FULL:v3p576/r3.anchor: قال القرظي: تدبرتها في القرآن فإذا هم المنافقون، فوجدتها: {ومن الناس من يعجبك قوله في الحياة الدنيا

TAB-FULL:v3p576/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p576/r4.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v3p576/r4.claim: Qatāda identifies the person described as a hypocrite.
TAB-FULL:v3p576/r4.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: " {ومن الناس من يعجبك قوله في الحياة الدنيا

TAB-FULL:v3p576#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p576#2/r1.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v3p576#2/r1.claim: Mujāhid explains the speech that pleases as the person’s outward public presentation in worldly life.
TAB-FULL:v3p576#2/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد: " {ومن الناس من يعجبك قوله} [البقرة: 204] قال: علانيته في الدنيا

TAB-FULL:v3p576#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p576#2/r2.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v3p576#2/r2.claim: Mujāhid reads the phrase as the person asserting during a dispute that he seeks the truth.
TAB-FULL:v3p576#2/r2.anchor: عن مجاهد: " {ومن الناس من يعجبك قوله} [البقرة: 204] قال: علانيته في الدنيا، {ويشهد الله} [البقرة: 204] في الخصومة

TAB-FULL:v3p576#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p576#2/r3.speaker: الربيع
TAB-FULL:v3p576#2/r3.claim: Al-Rabīʿ describes a servant whose speech is good but deeds are bad: he speaks pleasingly to the Messenger, then leaves to cause corruption.
TAB-FULL:v3p576#2/r3.anchor: عن الربيع، قوله: " {ومن الناس من يعجبك قوله في الحياة الدنيا ويشهد الله

TAB-FULL:v3p576#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p576#2/r4.speaker: عطاء
TAB-FULL:v3p576#2/r4.claim: ʿAṭāʾ says the speaker’s words differ from what is in his heart, which God knows.
TAB-FULL:v3p576#2/r4.anchor: عن ابن جريج، قال: قلت لعطاء: " {ومن الناس من يعجبك قوله في الحياة الدنيا ويشهد الله

TAB-FULL:v3p576#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p576#2/r5.speaker: عامة القراء
TAB-FULL:v3p576#2/r5.claim: The majority reading makes the hypocrite call God as witness that his profession agrees with his belief in God and His Messenger, although he lies.
TAB-FULL:v3p576#2/r5.anchor: فقرأته عامة القراء: {ويشهد الله على ما في قلبه}

TAB-FULL:v3p576#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p576#2/r6.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v3p576#2/r6.claim: Ibn Zayd recounts a hypocrite telling the Prophet that his heart matched his truthful-sounding words, then links the claim to 63:1, which calls the hypocrites liars in their testimony.
TAB-FULL:v3p576#2/r6.anchor: قال ابن زيد: " {ومن الناس من يعجبك قوله في الحياة الدنيا} [البقرة: 204] إلى

TAB-FULL:v3p578/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p578/r1.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v3p578/r1.claim: Al-Suddī explains the speaker’s claim as: God knows that I am truthful and intend to become Muslim.
TAB-FULL:v3p578/r1.anchor: وقال السدي: " {ويشهد الله على ما في قلبه}

TAB-FULL:v3p578/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p578/r2.speaker: ابن محيصن
TAB-FULL:v3p578/r2.claim: Ibn Muḥayṣin reads God as the witness to the hypocrisy hidden in the person’s heart and to the lie concealed beneath his public words; Ibn ʿAbbās adopted this sense.
TAB-FULL:v3p578/r2.anchor: وهي قراءة ابن محيصن، وعلى ذلك المعنى تأوله ابن عباس

TAB-FULL:v3p578/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p578/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v3p578/r3.claim: Al-Ṭabarī prefers the majority reading, where the hypocrite calls God as witness to his inward sincerity, because the authoritative readers agree on it.
TAB-FULL:v3p578/r3.anchor: والذي نختار في ذلك من قول القراء قراءة من قرأ: {ويشهد الله على ما في قلبه} [البقرة: 204] بمعنى يستشهد الله

TAB-FULL:v3p578#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p578#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v3p578#2/r1.claim: Al-add describes a man fierce in disputation; the forms lidad and ladāda describe being contentious, while ladda someone describes prevailing over an opponent.
TAB-FULL:v3p578#2/r1.anchor: الرجال: الشديد الخصومة، يقال في «فعلت» منه

TAB-FULL:v3p578#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p578#2/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v3p578#2/r2.claim: An unnamed rajaz poet’s line uses taluddu for defeating fierce opponents, supporting the sense of overpowering an adversary.
TAB-FULL:v3p578#2/r2.anchor: ثم أردي بهم من تردي … تلد أقران الخصوم اللد

TAB-FULL:v3p578#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p578#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v3p578#2/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses the phrase as argumentative when someone addresses and answers him.
TAB-FULL:v3p578#2/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس: " {وهو ألد الخصام} [البقرة: 204] أي ذو جدال

TAB-FULL:v3p578#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p578#2/r4.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v3p578#2/r4.claim: Qatāda describes a hard-hearted sinner who argues falsely, has a knowledgeable tongue but ignorant deeds, speaks wisdom, and acts sinfully.
TAB-FULL:v3p578#2/r4.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: " {وهو ألد الخصام} [البقرة: 204] يقول: شديد القسوة

TAB-FULL:v3p578#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p578#2/r5.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v3p578#2/r5.claim: Mujāhid says the person is unjust and does not conduct a dispute straight.
TAB-FULL:v3p578#2/r5.anchor: عن مجاهد: " {وهو ألد الخصام} [البقرة: 204] قال: ظالم لا يستقيم

TAB-FULL:v3p578#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p578#2/r6.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v3p578#2/r6.claim: Al-Suddī interprets the phrase as crooked contention.
TAB-FULL:v3p578#2/r6.anchor: عن السدي: " ألد الخصام: أعوج الخصام "

TAB-FULL:v3p578#2/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p578#2/r7.speaker: الحسن
TAB-FULL:v3p578#2/r7.claim: Al-Ḥasan says the phrase means lying in speech; al-Ṭabarī treats this as compatible with false, crooked argument.
TAB-FULL:v3p578#2/r7.anchor: عن الحسن، قال: " الألد الخصام: الكاذب القول

TAB-FULL:v3p578#2/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p578#2/r8.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v3p578#2/r8.claim: Al-Ṭabarī regards crookedness and false argument as closely related: distortion in disputation is itself contentious argument departing from truth.
TAB-FULL:v3p578#2/r8.anchor: وكلا هذين القولين متقارب المعنى، لأن الاعوجاج في الخصومة من الجدال، واللدد

TAB-FULL:v3p578#2/r9.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p578#2/r9.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v3p578#2/r9.claim: Al-Ṭabarī identifies khiṣām as the verbal noun of khāṣamtu, to dispute with someone.
TAB-FULL:v3p578#2/r9.anchor: وأما الخصام: فهو مصدر من قول القائل: خاصمت فلانا خصاما، ومخاصمة

TAB-FULL:v3p578#2/r10.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p578#2/r10.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v3p578#2/r10.claim: The verse reports that the hypocrite’s appealing speech and invocation of God accompany intense disputation based on false and deceitful speech.
TAB-FULL:v3p578#2/r10.anchor: وهذا خبر من الله تبارك وتعالى عن المنافق الذي أخبر نبيه محمدا صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه يعجبه إذا تكلم قيله

TAB-FULL:v3p588/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p588/r4.speaker: علي
TAB-FULL:v3p588/r4.claim: Asked about the passage extending through “God is kind to His servants,” ʿAlī replies, “By the Lord of the Kaʿba, the two fought,” referring to the contrasting figures in 2:204–207.
TAB-FULL:v3p588/r4.anchor: قال: سمعت عليا، في هذه الآية: " {ومن الناس من يعجبك قوله في الحياة الدنيا} [البقرة: 204] إلى

TABATABAI:2:204-206/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:204-206/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:204-206/r1.claim: These verses classify people by hypocrisy versus sincerity in faith, whereas the preceding verses classify them by whether they seek this world or the next; the connection to the Hajj verses is clear.
TABATABAI:2:204-206/r1.anchor: تشتمل الآيات على تقسيم آخر للناس من حيث نتائج صفاتهم، كما أن الآيات السابقة

TABATABAI:2:204-206/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:204-206/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:204-206/r2.claim: The phrase ‘in worldly life’ grammatically modifies ‘pleases you’: the speech pleases in this life because judgment here rests on appearances.
TABATABAI:2:204-206/r2.anchor: وقوله { في الحياة الدنيا } ، متعلق بقوله { يعجبك }

TABATABAI:2:204-206/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:204-206/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:204-206/r3.claim: People cannot see inner realities directly while living in this world; they can infer something of them only from their effects.
TABATABAI:2:204-206/r3.anchor: وأما الباطن والسريرة فتحت الستر ووراء الحجاب، لا يشاهده الإنسان

TABATABAI:2:204-206/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:204-206/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:204-206/r4.claim: The hypocrite speaks attractively of upholding truth, caring for people, and advancing religion and the community, yet is truth’s fiercest opponent.
TABATABAI:2:204-206/r4.anchor: يتكلم بما يعجبك كلامه، من ما يشير به إلى رعاية جانب الحق، والعناية بصلاح الخلق

TABATABAI:2:204-206/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:204-206/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:204-206/r5.claim: Ald is the superlative of l-d-d, ‘to contend fiercely’; al-khiṣām means severe disputation, with akhṣām as the plural of khaṣm.
TABATABAI:2:204-206/r5.anchor: أفعل التفضيل من لد لدودا إذا اشتد خصومة، والخصام جمع خصم كصعب وصعاب

TABATABAI:2:204-206/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:204-206/r6.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:2:204-206/r6.claim: An alternative grammatical account treats khiṣām as a verbal noun rather than a plural.
TABATABAI:2:204-206/r6.anchor: وقيل الخصام مصدر، ومعنى ألد الخصام أشد خصومة

TABRISI:2:204-205/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:204-205/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:204-205/r1.claim: Iʿjāb is pleasure in admiring what one finds pleasing; related forms describe wonder, particularly at exceptional beauty.
TABRISI:2:204-205/r1.anchor: الإعجاب هو سرور المعجب بما يستحسن ومنه العجب بالنفس

TABRISI:2:204-205/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:204-205/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:204-205/r2.claim: Aladd describes one who is difficult to overcome in dispute; related ladeed can mean the two sides of a valley or anything's two sides.
TABRISI:2:204-205/r2.anchor: إذا غلبه في الخصومة ولد الدواء في حلقه

TABRISI:2:204-205/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:204-205/r3.speaker: الزجاج
TABRISI:2:204-205/r3.claim: Al-Zajjāj takes khiṣām as the plural of khaṣm; adjectives on this pattern pluralize as fiʿāl, while nouns use afʿul in the few and fiʿāl in the many.
TABRISI:2:204-205/r3.anchor: والخصام قيل إنه جمع الخصم عن الزجاج وفعل إذا كان صفة فإنه يجمع على فعال

TABRISI:2:204-205/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:204-205/r4.speaker: الخليل
TABRISI:2:204-205/r4.claim: Al-Khalīl instead treats khiṣām as a verbal noun synonymous with mukhāṣama, disputation.
TABRISI:2:204-205/r4.anchor: وقيل الخصام مصدر كالمخاصمة عن الخليل

TABRISI:2:204-205/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:204-205/r12.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:2:204-205/r12.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the three verses were revealed about a hypocritical pretender who outwardly displays what he inwardly opposes.
TABRISI:2:204-205/r12.anchor: قال ابن عباس نزلت الآيات الثلاثة في المرائي

TABRISI:2:204-205/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:204-205/r13.speaker: الصادق
TABRISI:2:204-205/r13.claim: A report from al-Ṣādiq also identifies the verses' referent as a particular person, without naming him here.
TABRISI:2:204-205/r13.anchor: وهو المروي عن الصادق ع إلا أنه عين المعني به

TABRISI:2:204-205/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:204-205/r14.speaker: الحسن
TABRISI:2:204-205/r14.claim: Al-Ḥasan says the verses were revealed about the hypocrites generally.

TABRISI:2:204-205/r15.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:204-205/r15.speaker: السدي
TABRISI:2:204-205/r15.claim: Al-Suddī identifies the referent as al-Akhnas ibn Shurayq, who displayed affection for the Prophet and Islam while concealing the opposite.
TABRISI:2:204-205/r15.anchor: وقال السدي: نزلت في الأخنس بن شريق وكان يظهر الجميل بالنبي

TABRISI:2:204-205/r16.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:204-205/r16.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:204-205/r16.claim: The passage turns from the previously described believers and unbelievers to the condition of hypocrites.
TABRISI:2:204-205/r16.anchor: ثم بين سبحانه حال المنافقين بعد ذكره أحوال المؤمنين والكافرين

TABRISI:2:204-205/r17.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:204-205/r17.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:204-205/r17.claim: The hypocrite's speech pleases Muhammad and makes a strong impression.
TABRISI:2:204-205/r17.anchor: أي تستحسن كلامه يا محمد ويعظم موقعه من قلبك

TABRISI:2:204-205/r18.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:204-205/r18.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:204-205/r18.claim: He says that he believes in Muhammad and is his companion, or makes similar claims.
TABRISI:2:204-205/r18.anchor: أي يقول آمنت بك وأنا صاحب لك ونحو ذلك

TABRISI:2:204-205/r19.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:204-205/r19.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:204-205/r19.claim: He calls God to witness that his words reflect his heart, although his heart actually contradicts them.
TABRISI:2:204-205/r19.anchor: أي يحلف بالله ويشهده على أنه مضمر ما يقول

TABRISI:2:204-205/r20.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:204-205/r20.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:204-205/r20.claim: He is the most relentless of disputants; if khiṣām is a verbal noun, the phrase means a fierce, false arguer.
TABRISI:2:204-205/r20.anchor: وهو أشد المخاصمين خصومة ومن قال إن الخصام مصدر

THALABI:v2p119#2/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p119#2/r1.speaker: الكلبي والسدي ومقاتل وعطاء
THALABI:v2p119#2/r1.claim: Al-Kalbi, al-Suddi, Muqatil, and Ata say the verse concerns al-Akhnas ibn Shariq, a polished hypocrite who professed love for Muhammad, withdrew Banu Zuhra at Badr, then destroyed crops and livestock.
THALABI:v2p119#2/r1.anchor: الكلبي والسدي ومقاتل وعطاء: قالوا نزلت هذه الآية في الأخنس بن شريق الثقفي

THALABI:v2p120/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p120/r1.speaker: ابن عباس والضحاك
THALABI:v2p120/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas and al-Dahhak say verses through Allah's compassion to servants concern the Raji expedition: Quraysh lured six Muslims with a false conversion request, ambushed them, killed three, and captured Khubayb and Zayd.
THALABI:v2p120/r1.anchor: ابن عباس والضحاك: نزلت هذه الآيات إلى قوله والله رؤف بالعباد في سرية [الرجيع]

THALABI:v2p120/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p120/r2.speaker: ابن عباس والضحاك
THALABI:v2p120/r2.claim: In the Raji account, Aasim fought until captured; bees protected his corpse, then rain and a flood carried it away, fulfilling his vow never to touch or be touched by a polytheist. Umar marveled at God's protection.
THALABI:v2p120/r2.anchor: ابن عباس والضحاك: نزلت هذه الآيات إلى قوله والله رؤف بالعباد في سرية [الرجيع]

THALABI:v2p120/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p120/r3.speaker: ابن عباس والضحاك
THALABI:v2p120/r3.claim: The same account praises Khubayb's conduct in captivity: he borrowed a razor, safely held a child while armed, refused treachery, and was miraculously given fruit in Mecca.
THALABI:v2p120/r3.anchor: ابن عباس والضحاك: نزلت هذه الآيات إلى قوله والله رؤف بالعباد في سرية [الرجيع]

THALABI:v2p121/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p121/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v2p121/r1.claim: The narrative records Khubayb's poem that he did not care which side he fell on for God's cause, and his prayer that God count and scatter his executioners; the author glosses شلو ممزع as dismembered.
THALABI:v2p121/r1.anchor: ولست أبالي حين أقتل مسلما … على أي شق كان في الله مصرعي

THALABI:v2p121/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p121/r3.speaker: ابن عباس والضحاك
THALABI:v2p121/r3.claim: Zayd, whom Safwan bought to avenge his father, said he would not wish even a thorn to hurt Muhammad in exchange for being safe with his family; Abu Sufyan marveled at the Companions' love for Muhammad.
THALABI:v2p121/r3.anchor: فقال أبو سفيان لزيد حين قدم ليقتل أنشدك الله يا زيد أتحب أن محمدا عندنا الآن بمكانك

THALABI:v2p121/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p121/r6.speaker: author
THALABI:v2p121/r6.claim: After hypocrites reproached the martyrs, the verse was revealed about al-Zubayr, al-Miqdad, Khubayb, and their believing companions, and against those hypocrites.
THALABI:v2p121/r6.anchor: فأنزل الله في الزبير والمقداد بن الأسود وحبيب وأصحابه المؤمنين وفيمن طعن عليهم من المنافقين

THALABI:v2p122/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p122/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v2p122/r1.claim: Here يعجبك conveys approval and love for good-sounding speech; for disapproval one says عجبت من كذا.
THALABI:v2p122/r1.anchor: فقال في الخبر الاستحسان والمحبة: أعجبني كذا، وفي الإنكار والكراهية: عجبت من كذا

THALABI:v2p122/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p122/r2.speaker: المفضل
THALABI:v2p122/r2.claim: Al-Mufaddal says wonder originally concerns something without a like.
THALABI:v2p122/r2.anchor: وأصل العجب ما لم يكن مثله قاله المفضل.

THALABI:v2p122/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p122/r3.speaker: author
THALABI:v2p122/r3.claim: The hypocrite swears that he believes in and loves the Prophet, while concealing the opposite in his heart.
THALABI:v2p122/r3.anchor: يعني قول المنافق والله إني بك لمؤمن ولك محب.

THALABI:v2p122/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p122/r4.speaker: ابن محيصن
THALABI:v2p122/r4.claim: Ibn Muhaysin reads the verb with an open initial ya and ha and nominative ha; it means the man displays and says something while God knows his contrary intent.
THALABI:v2p122/r4.anchor: وقرأ ابن محيصن: ويشهد الله بفتح الياء والهاء ورفع الهاء من قوله

THALABI:v2p122/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p122/r5.speaker: أبي بن كعب
THALABI:v2p122/r5.claim: Ubayy's mushaf reads ويستشهد الله; the author cites this as evidence for the common reading.
THALABI:v2p122/r5.anchor: وفي مصحف أبي ويستشهد الله وهي حجة لقراءة العامة.

THALABI:v2p122/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p122/r6.speaker: author
THALABI:v2p122/r6.claim: ألد الخصام means extremely combative in dispute; al-Zajjaj derives ألد from the two sides of the neck, since the person prevails whichever direction an argument turns.
THALABI:v2p122/r6.anchor: وقال الزجاج: اشتقاقه من لديدي العنق وهما صفحتاه وتأويله إنه في أي وجه أخذ

THALABI:v2p122/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p122/r7.speaker: author
THALABI:v2p122/r7.claim: The root is used for a fierce opponent: لدد describes arguing and overcoming an adversary, and the forms apply to men, women, and groups.
THALABI:v2p122/r7.anchor: يقال منه لددت يا هذا وأنت تلد لدا ولداد، وإذا أردت إنه غلب خصمه

THALABI:v2p122/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p122/r8.speaker: الشاعر
THALABI:v2p122/r8.claim: An unnamed poet uses ألد for a formidable disputant in a line about a man of resolve and generosity beneath the stones.
THALABI:v2p122/r8.anchor: قال الشاعر: إن تحت الأحجار حزما وجودا … وخصيما ألد ذا مغلاق

THALABI:v2p122/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p122/r9.speaker: الراجز
THALABI:v2p122/r9.claim: The rajaz poet uses the root in تلد أقران الرجال اللد as evidence for the word's sense.
THALABI:v2p122/r9.anchor: وقال الراجز: تلد أقران الرجال اللد.

THALABI:v2p122/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p122/r10.speaker: author
THALABI:v2p122/r10.claim: The Quran also uses لدا for a people being warned, linking the word to severe disputation.
THALABI:v2p122/r10.anchor: قال الله تعالى وتنذر به قوما لدا .

THALABI:v2p122/r11.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p122/r11.speaker: أبو عبيدة
THALABI:v2p122/r11.claim: Abu Ubayda takes الخصام as the verbal noun of خاصمته, meaning disputation.
THALABI:v2p122/r11.anchor: والخصام: مصدر خاصمته خصاما ومخاصمة قاله أبو عبيدة

THALABI:v2p122/r12.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p122/r12.speaker: الزجاج
THALABI:v2p122/r12.claim: Al-Zajjaj reads الخصام as a plural of خصم, like بحر with بحار or بحور.
THALABI:v2p122/r12.anchor: وقال الزجاج: هو جمع خصم يقال: خصم وخصام وخصوم مثل بحر وبحار وبحور

THALABI:v2p122/r13.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p122/r13.speaker: author
THALABI:v2p122/r13.claim: The essence of disputation is excessive probing and pressure about a matter; the corners of vessels are therefore called خصوم.
THALABI:v2p122/r13.anchor: وحقيقة الخصومة التعمق في البحث عن الشيء والمضايقه فيه ولذلك قيل لزوايا الأوعية خصوم.

THALABI:v2p122/r14.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p122/r14.speaker: السدي
THALABI:v2p122/r14.claim: Al-Suddi glosses the expression as crooked disputation.
THALABI:v2p122/r14.anchor: قال السدي: ألد الخصام أعوج الخصام.

THALABI:v2p122/r15.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p122/r15.speaker: مجاهد
THALABI:v2p122/r15.claim: Mujahid describes the person as persistent and unrelenting in argument.

THALABI:v2p122/r16.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p122/r16.speaker: الحسن
THALABI:v2p122/r16.claim: Al-Hasan says he is a liar in his speech.

THALABI:v2p122/r17.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p122/r17.speaker: قتادة
THALABI:v2p122/r17.claim: Qatada describes him as hard-hearted in disobedience, disputing falsely, eloquent but ignorant in action, speaking wisdom while committing sin.
THALABI:v2p122/r17.anchor: قتادة: هو شديد القسوة في معصية الله جدل بالباطل عالم باللسان

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p74/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p74/r1.speaker: الكلبي والسدي ومقاتل وابن عباس في رواية عطاء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p74/r1.claim: They say the verse was revealed about al-Akhnas ibn Shurayq, called Akhnas because he withdrew with 300 men of Banu Zuhra from Badr; he charmed the Prophet, professed Islam and love, swore sincerity, and was a hypocrite inwardly.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p74/r1.anchor: قال الكلبي (¬1) والسدي (¬2) ومقاتل (¬3) وابن عباس (¬4)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p74/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p74/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p74/r2.claim: The qualification in worldly life reflects his lying: the Prophet was not truly impressed with his words, and al-Akhnas earns no afterlife reward for them.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p74/r2.anchor: لأنه كاذب، فما تعجب النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - من كلامه (¬8)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p75/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p75/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p75/r1.claim: He swears that he believes and loves the Prophet and claims God witnesses this inward faith, but he lies; the intended sense is faith in his own claim.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p75/r1.anchor: فهو يحلف بالله ويشهده على أنه مضمر (¬2) ما يقوله، وهو كاذب

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p75/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p75/r2.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p75/r2.claim: Al-add means intensely quarrelsome; Abu Ishaq derives it from the two sides of the neck, since the man prevails whichever side of an argument he takes.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p75/r2.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق: أخذ من لديدي العنق، وهما صفحتاه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p75/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p75/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p75/r3.claim: Al-khisam is a verbal noun like mukhasama, from quarrelsomeness; disputation probes and constricts an issue, and vessel corners are called khusum, singular khasm.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p75/r3.anchor: والخصام: مصدر، كالمخاصمة، والمخاصمة: مفاعلة من الخصومة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p75/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p75/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p75/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas explains the phrase as a person who abandons the truth and argues for falsehood.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p75/r4.anchor: قال ابن عباس في قوله: {ألد الخصام} يريد: الذي يدع الحق

QASHANI:2:204-205/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:2:204-205/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:2:204-205/r1.claim: Qashani quotes a saying: give sinners glad tidings that God forgives, and warn the righteous that God forgives.
QASHANI:2:204-205/r1.anchor: بشر المذنبين بأني غفور وأنذر الصديقين بأني غفور

QASHANI:2:204-205/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:2:204-205/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:2:204-205/r2.claim: The person whose speech pleases claims love while being a fierce opponent, since he remains in the lower self and heresy; he speaks only in worldly life, not from the heart in the afterlife.
QASHANI:2:204-205/r2.anchor: يدعي المحبة وهو ألد الخصام لكونه في مقام النفس زنديقا

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:203-204/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:203-204/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:203-204/r5.claim: The person is al-Akhnas ibn Shariq, a hypocrite with smooth speech and a good public face but evil inward character.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:203-204/r5.anchor: { ومن الناس من يعجبك قوله... } الآية. يعني: الأخنس بن شريق، وكان منافقا حلو الكلام، حسن العلانية سيىء السريرة،

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:203-204/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:203-204/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:203-204/r6.claim: His speech impresses people only in worldly life and earns no reward in the Hereafter.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:203-204/r6.anchor: { في الحياة الدنيا } لأن قوله إنما يعجب الناس في الحياة الدنيا، ولا ثواب له عليه في الآخرة

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:203-204/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:203-204/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:203-204/r7.claim: Al-Akhnas used to swear to the Prophet that he believed in him and loved him.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:203-204/r7.anchor: { ويشهد الله على ما في قلبه } لأنه كان يقول للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: والله، إني بك لمؤمن، ولك محب

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:203-204/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:203-204/r8.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:203-204/r8.claim: He is fierce in disputation and argues falsely.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:203-204/r8.anchor: { وهو ألد الخصام } أي: شديد الخصومة، وكان جدلا بالباطل.

ELMALILI:2:203-207/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:203-207/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:203-207/r13.claim: Some people impress the listener with worldly talk and invoke God as witness to their heart, using oaths and smooth words to deceive.
ELMALILI:2:203-207/r13.anchor: onun hayât-ı dünyâ zımnındaki lakırdısı senin taaccübünü celb eder ve pek beğenecek olursun {وَيُشْهِدُ ٱللَّهَ عَلَىٰ مَا فِى قَلْبِهِۦ} o kalbindekine Allah’ı şâhid de tutar

ELMALILI:2:203-207/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:203-207/r14.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:203-207/r14.claim: Despite his pleasing words, he is in truth an intensely hostile and ruthless opponent, as is typical of wicked people.
ELMALILI:2:203-207/r14.anchor: hâlbuki hakikatte onun düşmanlığı kıyaktır. Ve zaten habis olan kimselerin düşmanlığı pek kıyak, pek gaddar olur.

ELMALILI:2:203-207/r20.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:203-207/r20.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:203-207/r20.claim: The verses were revealed about Ahnes ibn Sharik of Banu Thaqif, an ally of Banu Zuhra, who professed Islam and love to the Prophet, then burned a Muslim field and killed livestock after leaving.
ELMALILI:2:203-207/r20.anchor: Bu âyetler, Benî Sakîf’ten Ahnes b. Şerîk hakkında nâzil olmuştur.

ELMALILI:2:203-207/r21.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:203-207/r21.speaker: müfessirînin ekser-i muhakkikīni
ELMALILI:2:203-207/r21.claim: Most authoritative exegetes say the passage applies generally to all hypocrites who display these traits, not only its specific occasion.
ELMALILI:2:203-207/r21.anchor: mazmûn-ı âyet bu gibi evsâf ile muttasıf olan münafıkların hepsine şâmil olduğunu müfessirînin ekser-i muhakkikīni tasrih etmişlerdir.

ELMALILI:2:203-207/r22.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:203-207/r22.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:203-207/r22.claim: The passage teaches that people considered for positions of responsibility should be assessed by their conduct, not merely their words.
ELMALILI:2:203-207/r22.anchor: insanların dillerine bakılmayıp hâllerinin tedkīki lüzûmunu iş‘âr için nâstan üçüncü bir kısmın hisâlini göstermiştir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:204/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:204/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:204/r1.claim: These verses revisit the earlier contrast between people seeking only worldly benefit and those seeking good in both this world and the afterlife.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:204/r1.anchor: Yukarıda biri yalnız dünyayı isteyen, diğeri de hem dünyanın hem de âhiretin iyiliklerini isteyen

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:204/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:204/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:204/r2.claim: One human type speaks attractively but has evil intent and acts as a corrupter and destroyer.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:204/r2.anchor: Bunlardan biri güzel sözlü fakat kötü niyetli, bozguncu ve yıkıcıdır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:204/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:204/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:204/r4.claim: Reports connect the revelation to hypocrites who appeared friendly before the Prophet and acted destructively behind his back.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:204/r4.anchor: Bazı münafıkların Hz. Peygamber’in yanında dost gibi gözüküp arkasından yıkıcı hareketlerde bulunmaları üzerine bu âyetlerin indiği yolunda rivayetler

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:204/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:204/r5.speaker: Râzî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:204/r5.claim: Razi says the verses censure bad qualities rather than particular people, so anyone bearing those qualities deserves censure.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:204/r5.anchor: Râzî’nin de belirttiği gibi Allah Teâlâ bir topluluğu, bazı kötü niteliklerini göstererek yerdiğinde, bundan o kişilerin zatını değil niteliklerini yerdiği anlamı çıkar

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:204/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:204/r6.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:204/r6.claim: Even if the verses originally concerned one or several hypocrites in the Prophet’s time, their warning applies to everyone who adopts hypocrisy, ostentation, corruption, or destruction.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:204/r6.anchor: bu âyetler Hz. Peygamber dönemindeki belli bir veya birkaç münafık hakkında inmiş olsa bile münafıklık, riyakârlık, bozgunculuk, tahripçilik gibi kötü huy ve davranışlar konusunda bütün insanlar için bir uyarı

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:204/r8.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:204/r8.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:204/r8.claim: Hypocritical and ostentatious people flatter others and invoke God as witness, then after leaving or gaining office act from enmity and damage livelihoods and descendants.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:204/r8.anchor: Riyakâr veya münafık tabiatlı kişiler genellikle insanın yanında hoşa gidecek sözler söyler, sözlerinin doğruluğuna Allah’ı şahit bile koşarlar

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:204/r11.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:204/r11.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:204/r11.claim: Although Muslims should generally think well of people, this passage warns that good opinion does not mean credulously trusting every claim or smiling face.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:204/r11.anchor: Hucurât sûresinde de bildirildiği üzere (bk. 49/12) müslümanların genellikle insanlar hakkında hüsnüzan beslemeleri esas olmakla birlikte konumuz olan âyetler

BAQILLANI:v1p31/r1.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p31/r1.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p31/r1.claim: The Torah, Gospel, and other scriptures are not inimitable in composition, though they may share the Qur’an’s inimitability in reporting unseen matters.
BAQILLANI:v1p31/r1.anchor: ليس شيء من ذلك بمعجز في النظم والتأليف وإن كان معجزا كالقرآن فيما يتضمن من الإخبار عن الغيوب

BAQILLANI:v1p31/r2.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p31/r2.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p31/r2.claim: He argues other languages permit less eloquent differentiation: they have fewer names for one thing, less polysemy, and less scope for metaphor, allusion, and varied usage.
BAQILLANI:v1p31/r2.anchor: لا نعرف فيها الكلمة الواحدة تتناول المعاني الكثيرة على ما تتناوله العربية وكذلك التصرف في الاستعارات والإشارات

BAQILLANI:v1p31/r3.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p31/r3.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p31/r3.claim: The Qur’an’s repeated description as clear Arabic, and its being kept from a foreign tongue, support the special eloquence of Arabic; intelligibility to its first hearers may also be a benefit.
BAQILLANI:v1p31/r3.anchor: ويشهد لذلك من القرآن أن الله تعالى وصفه بأنه

BAQILLANI:v1p31/r4.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p31/r4.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p31/r4.claim: Muslims skilled in both Arabic and other languages recognize that the latter lack Arabic’s degrees of eloquence and stylistic distinction.
BAQILLANI:v1p31/r4.anchor: قد عرفوا تلك الألسنة وهم من أهل البراعة فيها وفي العربية فقد وقفوا على أنه ليس فيها من التفاضل والفصاحة

BAQILLANI:v1p31/r5.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p31/r5.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p31/r5.claim: The Qur’an’s unique inimitability is confirmed by the fact that neither scriptural communities nor Muslims claimed it for the Torah or Gospel.
BAQILLANI:v1p31/r5.anchor: لم نجد أهل التوراة والإنجيل ادعوا الإعجاز لكتابهم ولا ادعى لهم المسلمون

BAQILLANI:v1p155/r1.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p155/r1.speaker: أفضل من رأيت من أهل العلم بالأدب
BAQILLANI:v1p155/r1.claim: An eminent specialist says prose can accommodate greater eloquence than poetry because poetic form constrains speech and its development.
BAQILLANI:v1p155/r1.anchor: أفضل من رأيت من أهل العلم بالأدب والحذق بهذه الصناعة مع تقدمه في الكلام يقول

BAQILLANI:v1p155/r2.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p155/r2.speaker: من يتقدم في صنعة الكلام
BAQILLANI:v1p155/r2.claim: A skilled interlocutor counters that poetry may be more eloquent when it meets the conditions of eloquence and includes the causes of rhetorical beauty.
BAQILLANI:v1p155/r2.anchor: وحضره من يتقدم في صنعة الكلام فراجعه في ذلك وذكر أنه لا يمتنع أن يكون الشعر أبلغ

BAQILLANI:v1p155/r3.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p155/r3.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p155/r3.claim: The author sides with the poetry view: most Arab verbal brilliance is in poetry, while prose lacks comparable examples, despite the later refinement of letters.
BAQILLANI:v1p155/r3.anchor: ويشهد عندي للقول الأخير أن معظم براعة كلام العرب في الشعر

BAQILLANI:v1p155/r4.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p155/r4.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p155/r4.claim: Although poetry narrows expression, it gathers and joins its parts; when fully polished in its genre, no human speech can rival it.
BAQILLANI:v1p155/r4.anchor: وهو وإن ضيق نطاق القول فهو يجمع حواشيه ويضم أطرافه ونواحيه

BAQILLANI:v1p155/r5.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p155/r5.speaker: المتنبي
BAQILLANI:v1p155/r5.claim: A report says al-Mutanabbi’s companion questioned his Qur’an reading; his reply that the eloquent Meccan was silenced would, if authentic, show his belief in poetry’s greater eloquence.
BAQILLANI:v1p155/r5.anchor: عن المتنبي انه كان ينظر في المصحف

BAQILLANI:v1p155/r6.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p155/r6.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p155/r6.claim: To show the Qur’an’s superiority, he proposes examining an acclaimed, well-made poem for flaws, uneven structure, digressions, forced phrasing, and shifts between elevated and low diction.
BAQILLANI:v1p155/r6.anchor: على مواضع خللها وعلى تفاوت نظمها وعلى اختلاف فصولها وعلى كثرة فضولها

BURHAN:v1p157/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p157/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p157/r2.claim: The general, unnamed wording ‘among people is one whose speech pleases you’ exemplifies veiling a person’s identity, which can make admonition more effective in winning his sympathy.
BURHAN:v1p157/r2.anchor: الثالث قصد الستر عليه ليكون أبلغ فى إستعطافه ولهذا كان النبى صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا بلغه عن قوم شيء خطب فقال ما بال رجال

BURHAN:v1p157/r8.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p157/r8.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p157/r8.claim: The section lists this verse among Qur’anic examples that leave the offending person unnamed to preserve the possibility of winning him over.
BURHAN:v1p157/r8.anchor: ولهذا كان النبى صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا بلغه عن قوم شيء خطب فقال ما بال رجال

BURHAN:v3p382/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p382/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p382/r1.claim: All eight pronouns in this verse agree with the singular wording of man, although the intended meaning is plural.
BURHAN:v3p382/r1.anchor: وقد يجرى الكلام على أوله في الإفراد

BURHAN:v3p382/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p382/r3.speaker: علم الدين العراقي
BURHAN:v3p382/r3.claim: At the meeting of literal and semantic agreement, starting with the literal form is usual; al-ʿIrāqī says only one Qur’anic passage begins with semantic agreement.
BURHAN:v3p382/r3.anchor: وما ذكرنا من البداءة باللفظ عند الاجتماع هو الكثير قال الشيخ علم الدين العراقي ولم يجيء في القرآن البداءة بالحمل على المعنى إلا في موضع واحد

BURHAN:v3p382/r7.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p382/r7.speaker: ابن عصفور
BURHAN:v3p382/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAṣfūr reports that Kufans require a separator between clauses when switching from agreement by meaning to agreement by form, whereas Basrans do not; Abū Ḥayyān says usage occurs only with a separator.
BURHAN:v3p382/r7.anchor: ولم يعتبر البصريون الفاصل قال ولم يرد السماع إلا بالفاصل كما ذهب إليه الكوفيون

BURHAN:v3p382/r9.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p382/r9.speaker: ابن عصفور
BURHAN:v3p382/r9.claim: Ibn ʿAṣfūr’s precise rule permits ‘those who rise today and look after our affairs, our brothers’ but bars the same sequence without today as a separator; he says transmitted usage has the separator.
BURHAN:v3p382/r9.anchor: شرط الكوفيون في جواز اعتبار اللفظ بعد اعتبار المعنى الفصل

BURHAN:v1p212/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p212/r1.speaker: ابن العربي
BURHAN:v1p212/r1.claim: Ibn al-ʿArabī says no text or report specifies what the seven are, and scholars have differed over their identification.
BURHAN:v1p212/r1.anchor: وقال ابن العربى لم يأت فى معنى هذا السبع نص ولا أثر واختلف الناس فى تعيينها

BURHAN:v1p212/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p212/r2.speaker: أبو حاتم بن حبان
BURHAN:v1p212/r2.claim: Abū Ḥātim ibn Ḥibbān counted thirty-five opinions; one group sees the seven as facilitation for reciters rather than a limiting number, while most hold that they are exactly seven.
BURHAN:v1p212/r2.anchor: وقال الحافظ أبو حاتم بن حبان البستى اختلف الناس فيها على خمسة وثلاثين قولا وقال وقفت منها على كثير فذهب بعضهم إلى أن المراد التوسعة على القارىء ولم يقصد به الحصر والأكثر على أنه محصور فى سبعة

BURHAN:v1p212/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p212/r3.speaker: أبو حاتم بن حبان
BURHAN:v1p212/r3.claim: Those who limit the seven disagree whether they remain available to read now or applied only at the beginning.
BURHAN:v1p212/r3.anchor: ثم اختلفوا هل هى باقية إلى الآن نقرؤها أم كان ذلك أولا

BURHAN:v1p212/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p212/r4.speaker: القرطبي
BURHAN:v1p212/r4.claim: Al-Qurṭubī says most proponents of the view that the initial permission later settled on today’s reading include Sufyān ibn ʿUyayna, Ibn Wahb, al-Ṭabarī, and al-Ṭaḥāwī.
BURHAN:v1p212/r4.anchor: وقال القرطبى إن القائلين بالثانى وهو أن الأمر كان كذلك ثم استقر على ما هو الآن هم أكثر العلماء منهم سفيان بن عيينة وابن وهب والطبرى والطحاوى

BURHAN:v1p212/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p212/r5.speaker: أكثر العلماء
BURHAN:v1p212/r5.claim: Among those who hold that the permission settled into one reading, most say this happened during the Prophet’s lifetime; al-Bāqillānī, Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr, and Ibn al-ʿArabī chose that view.
BURHAN:v1p212/r5.anchor: ثم اختلفوا هل استقر فى حياته صلى الله عليه وسلم أم بعد وفاته والأكثرون على الأول واختاره القاضى أبو بكر بن الطيب وابن عبد البر وابن العربى

BURHAN:v1p212/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p212/r6.speaker: القاضي أبو بكر بن الطيب وابن عبد البر وابن العربي
BURHAN:v1p212/r6.claim: The initial allowance eased differences among Arab dialects; as speakers trained and one form sufficed, God abrogated the permission after Gabriel reviewed the Qur’an twice with the Prophet in the final year.
BURHAN:v1p212/r6.anchor: ورأوا أن ضرورة اختلاف لغات العرب ومشقة نطقهم

BURHAN:v1p226/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p226/r1.speaker: بعض المتأخرين
BURHAN:v1p226/r1.claim: Some later scholars take the seven aḥruf to mean dialects, allowing Arab groups to use their customary pronunciations, such as assimilation, imāla, emphatic articulation, hamza, softening, and lengthening.
BURHAN:v1p226/r1.anchor: وقال بعض المتأخرين الأشبه بظواهر الأحاديث أن المراد بهذه الأحرف اللغات وهو أن يقرأ كل قوم من العرب بلغتهم وما جرت عليه عادتهم من الإظهار والإدغام

BURHAN:v1p226/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p226/r3.speaker: بعض المتأخرين
BURHAN:v1p226/r3.claim: On this view the seven aḥruf are the seven canonical readings, all soundly transmitted from the Prophet and compiled in ʿUthmān’s codex; the seven reciters chose among the readings they knew, and each had more than one valid choice.
BURHAN:v1p226/r3.anchor: وهذه الوجوه هى القراءات السبع التى قرأها القراء السبعة فإنها كلها صحت عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وهو الذى جمع عليه عثمان المصحف

BURHAN:v1p226/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p226/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p226/r4.claim: The source says Muslims in these generations agree to rely on what is soundly transmitted from the seven; the original allowance was mercy for people who would struggle to abandon their dialects.
BURHAN:v1p226/r4.anchor: وقد أجمع المسلمون فى هذه الأعصار على الاعتماد على ما صح عنهم وكان الإنزال على الأحرف السبعة توسعة من الله ورحمة على الأمة

BURHAN:v1p226/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p226/r5.speaker: أبي بن كعب
BURHAN:v1p226/r5.claim: A report from Ubayy ibn Kaʿb recounts Gabriel telling the Prophet, who was sent to an unlettered community including elderly people, children, and those who had never read a book, that the Qur’an was revealed on seven aḥruf; al-Tirmidhī grades it ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ.
BURHAN:v1p226/r5.anchor: ما رواه الترمذى عن أبى بن كعب أنه لقى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم جبريل فقال يا جبريل إنى بعثت إلى أمة أميين

BURHAN:v1p241/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p241/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p241/r1.claim: Many Companions memorized the Qur’an during the Prophet’s life, and every portion was memorized by numerous people, at least enough for mass transmission.
BURHAN:v1p241/r1.anchor: حفظه فى حياته جماعة من الصحابة وكل قطعة منه كان يحفظها جماعة كثيرة أقلهم بالغون حد التواتر

BURHAN:v1p241/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p241/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
BURHAN:v1p241/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports that when revelation came, the Prophet summoned scribes and directed where to place the verses; al-Tirmidhī calls the report ḥasan and al-Ḥākim ṣaḥīḥ by the two Shaykhs’ criteria.
BURHAN:v1p241/r2.anchor: وجاء فى ذلك أخبار ثابتة فى الترمذى والمستدرك وغيرهما من حديث ابن عباس قال كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يأتى عليه الزمان

BURHAN:v1p241/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p241/r3.speaker: أنس بن مالك
BURHAN:v1p241/r3.claim: In al-Bukhārī’s report from Anas, the four who compiled the Qur’an in the Prophet’s time were Ubayy, Muʿādh, Zayd ibn Thābit, and Abū Zayd; al-Bayhaqī prefers this report and Ibn Sīrīn names the same four without dispute.
BURHAN:v1p241/r3.anchor: وفى البخارى عن قتاده قال سألت أنس بن مالك من جمع القرآن على عهد رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال أربعة كلهم من الانصار

BURHAN:v1p241/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p241/r4.speaker: ابن سيرين
BURHAN:v1p241/r4.claim: Ibn Sīrīn’s report differs over two additional names, variously giving Abū al-Dardāʾ and ʿUthmān or ʿUthmān and Tamīm al-Dārī.
BURHAN:v1p241/r4.anchor: واختلفوا فى رجلين من ثلاثة أبو الدرداء وعثمان وقيل عثمان وتميم الدارى

BURHAN:v1p241/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p241/r5.speaker: الشعبي
BURHAN:v1p241/r5.claim: Al-Shaʿbī gives another list of compilers, saying Mujammaʿ ibn Jāriya had obtained all but two or three sūras; he adds that among the Prophet’s Companions only ʿUthmān among the caliphs compiled it.
BURHAN:v1p241/r5.anchor: وعن الشعبى جمعه ستة أبى وزيد ومعاذ وأبو الدرداء وسعد بن عبيد وأبو زيد ومجمع بن جارية قد أخذه إلا سورتين أو ثلاثة

BURHAN:v1p241/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p241/r6.speaker: أبو شامة
BURHAN:v1p241/r6.claim: Abū Shāma says al-Qāḍī Abū Bakr argued that far more people had collected the Qur’an in the Prophet’s lifetime; the large number of readers killed at Yamāma and Biʾr Maʿūna supports this.
BURHAN:v1p241/r6.anchor: وقد أشبع القاضي أبو بكر محمد بن الطيب في كتاب الانتصار الكلام في حملة القرآن في حياة النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وأقام الأدلة على أنهم كانوا أضعاف هذه العدة المذكورة

BURHAN:v1p241/r7.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p241/r7.speaker: القاضي أبو بكر
BURHAN:v1p241/r7.claim: One reconciliation is that the named few alone collected the Qur’an in all its revealed modes, aḥruf, and readings.
BURHAN:v1p241/r7.anchor: ومنها بتقرير سلامتها فالمعنى لم يجمعه على جميع الأوجه والأحرف والقراءات التى نزل به إلا أولئك النفر

BURHAN:v1p241/r8.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p241/r8.speaker: القاضي أبو بكر
BURHAN:v1p241/r8.claim: A second reconciliation is that only those Companions collected both material later abrogated and erased from writing and material whose written form and recitation remained obligatory.
BURHAN:v1p241/r8.anchor: أنه لم يجمع ما نسخ منه وأزيل رسمه بعد تلاوته

BURHAN:v1p241/r9.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p241/r9.speaker: القاضي أبو بكر
BURHAN:v1p241/r9.claim: A third reconciliation is that only those Companions received the entire Qur’an directly from the Prophet, collecting it from his recitation.
BURHAN:v1p241/r9.anchor: ومنها أنه لم يجمع جميع القرآن عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وأخذه من فيه تلقيا غير تلك الجماعة

BURHAN:v4p128/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p128/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p128/r3.claim: Fiʿl is the broadest among related verbs, applying to speech, thought, and other acts; ʿamal is narrower and covers intention, resolve, and speech.
BURHAN:v4p128/r3.anchor: ومن ذلك جعل وهي أحد الافعال المشتركة التي هي أمهات احداث وهي فعل وعمل وجعل وطفق وانشا واقبل واعمها فعل يقع على القول والهم وغيرهما

BURHAN:v4p128/r7.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p128/r7.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p128/r7.claim: Jaʿala may mean beginning or embarking, like kāda and ṭafiqa, with a sense of entering into the action: jaʿala yaqūlu means he began to speak.
BURHAN:v4p128/r7.anchor: الثاني بمعنى المقاربة مثل كاد وطفق لكنها تفيد ملابسة الفعل والشروع فيه تقول جعل يقول وجعل يفعل كذا اذا شرع فيه

ITQAN:v4p382#2/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p382#2/r2.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p382#2/r2.claim: Concealing an individual's name can protect him and make the description more effective in winning sympathy; the unnamed person here is al-Akhnas ibn Shurayq, who later became a good Muslim.
ITQAN:v4p382#2/r2.anchor: الثالث قصد الستر عليه ليكون أبلغ في إستعطافه نحو ﴿ ومن الناس من يعجبك قوله في الحياة الدنيا ﴾ الآية هو الأخنس بن شريق وقد أسلم بعد وحسن إسلامه

ITQAN:v4p382#2/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p382#2/r3.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p382#2/r3.claim: The unnamed man described as pleasing in speech in worldly life is al-Akhnas ibn Shurayq, who later embraced Islam and practiced it well.
ITQAN:v4p382#2/r3.anchor: هو الأخنس بن شريق وقد أسلم بعد وحسن إسلامه

ITQAN:v4p384/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p384/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p384/r1.claim: The science of Quranic ambiguities depends entirely on transmitted evidence; reason alone cannot identify their referents.
ITQAN:v4p384/r1.anchor: أعلم أن علم المبهمات مرجعه النقل المحض لا مجال للرأي فيه

ITQAN:v4p384/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p384/r2.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p384/r2.claim: Al-Suyuti says earlier works named ambiguous referents and disagreements without dependable attribution, so he compiled a source-traced work grading sound and weak reports.
ITQAN:v4p384/r2.anchor: ألفت الكتاب الذي ألفته مذكورا فيه عزو كل قول إلى قائله من الصحابة والتابعين وغيرهم معزوا إلى أصحاب الكتب الذين خرجوا ذلك بأسانيدهم مبينا فيه ما صح سنده وما ضعف

ITQAN:v4p384/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p384/r3.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p384/r3.claim: He arranged the book in Quran order and briefly divides ambiguities into two categories, beginning with specified persons and groups whose names are known.
ITQAN:v4p384/r3.anchor: وقد رتبته على ترتيب القرآن وأنا ألخص هنا مبهماته بأوجز عبارة تاركا العزو والتخريج غالبا إختصارا وإحالة على الكتاب المذكور وأرتبه على قسمين

ITQAN:v4p384/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p384/r9.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p384/r9.claim: The person whose speech impresses the listener is al-Akhnas ibn Shurayq.

ITQAN:v2p339#7/r33.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p339#7/r33.speaker: ابن عباس
ITQAN:v2p339#7/r33.claim: The phrase means fierce or vehement in disputation.

ITQAN:v2p369/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p369/r9.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p369/r9.claim: Ald al-khisam means disputation in falsehood; Muhalhil’s verse describes a fierce contentious opponent.
ITQAN:v2p369/r9.anchor: قال الجدل المخاصم في الباطل أما سمعت قول مهلهل

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p245/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p245/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p245/r1.claim: Unlike a poet who denies that a patron has fever, al-Mutanabbī imagines the fever daring to attack such a noble man and supplies an imagined excuse for its assault.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p245/r1.anchor: كأنه سال نفسه كيف اجترأت الحمى على الممدوح مع جلالته وهيبته

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p245/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p245/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p245/r2.claim: Ibn al-Muʿtazz's speaker denies that his gray hair is age, calling it battle dust; Jurjānī praises this concise denial as a direct way to escape reproach, rather than conceding and defending the grayness.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p245/r2.anchor: ألا تراه أنكر أن يكون الذي بدأ به شيبا ورأى الاعتصام بالجحد أخصر طريقا إلى نفى العيب

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p245/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p245/r3.speaker: الطائي الكبير
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p245/r3.claim: The poet recasts gray hair as the smile of reason and refinement, making a bodily sign of age into intellectual radiance.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p245/r3.anchor: ولا يروعك إيماض القتير به فإن ذاك إبتسام الرأي والأدب

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p245/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p245/r4.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p245/r4.claim: Simile can achieve a magical subtlety that plain description cannot reach, giving poetry unusual power to delight, console, and display eloquence.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p245/r4.anchor: وينبغي أن باب التشبيهات قد حظي من هذه الطريقة بضرب من السحر لا تأتي الصفة على غرابته

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p113/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p113/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p113/r1.claim: Announcing a subject through a pronoun and then explaining it is more emphatic than stating the proposition abruptly, because the advance notice acts like a repeated assertion.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p113/r1.anchor: ثم فسر كان ذلك أفخم له من أن يذكر من غير تقدم إضمار

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p113/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p113/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p113/r2.claim: This emphatic construction suits denials, suspicion, false claims, and surprising contradictions, as shown by Qur'anic examples where the added clause confirms or exposes what was disputed.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p113/r2.anchor: هذا الضرب من الكلام يجيء فيما سبق فيه إنكار من منكر

TUSTARI:2:204/r1.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:2:204/r1.speaker: author
TUSTARI:2:204/r1.claim: The phrase means someone intensely contentious in falsehood.

TUSTARI:2:204/r2.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:2:204/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
TUSTARI:2:204/r2.claim: Aisha reports the Prophet saying that the most hateful of men to God is the fiercely contentious adversary.
TUSTARI:2:204/r2.anchor: روت عائشة رضي الله عنها عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p40/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p40/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p40/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas relates that after a raid party including Asim and Mirthad was killed, two hypocrites disparaged them for dying instead of staying home or delivering the Prophet’s message; the verse followed.
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p40/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال لما أصيبت السرية التي فيها عاصم ومرثد قال رجلان من المنافقين

SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p40/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p40/r2.speaker: السدي
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p40/r2.claim: Al-Suddi identifies al-Akhnas ibn Shurayq: he professed Islam to the Prophet, then burned Muslims’ crops and hamstrung their donkeys, prompting the verse.
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p40/r2.anchor: عن السدي قال نزلت في الأخنس بن شريق أقبل إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p65/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p65/r3.speaker: السدي
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p65/r3.claim: Al-Suddi identifies the hypocritical speaker as al-Akhnas ibn Shariq: after professing sincerity to Muhammad, he burned Muslim crops and hamstrung their donkeys, prompting the next verse.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p65/r3.anchor: قال السدي نزلت في الأخنس بن شريق الثقفي، وهو حليف بني زهرة

AKHFASH:v1p178/r2.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p178/r2.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p178/r2.claim: The first construal has the person himself call God to witness what is in his heart.
AKHFASH:v1p178/r2.anchor: قال {ويشهد الله على ما فى قلبه} اذا كان هو يشهد

AKHFASH:v1p178/r3.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p178/r3.speaker: بعضهم
AKHFASH:v1p178/r3.claim: Another construal makes God the one who witnesses what is in the person's heart.
AKHFASH:v1p178/r3.anchor: وقال بعضهم: {ويشهد الله} أي إن الله هو الذي يشهد

AKHFASH:v1p178/r4.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p178/r4.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p178/r4.claim: Aladd is the intensive form from l-d-d, with the paradigms ladadtu/taluddu, a people called ludd, a woman laddāʾ, and women lud.
AKHFASH:v1p178/r4.anchor: من "لددت" "تلد" و"هو ألد" و"هم قوم لد"

FARRA:v1p123/r1.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p123/r1.speaker: author
FARRA:v1p123/r1.claim: The verse’s al-add term is illustrated by Arab use for a fierce disputant; the cited, unattributed line and forms ladda/ladadtuhu describe prevailing in argument.
FARRA:v1p123/r1.anchor: اللد أقران الرجال اللد ... ثم أردى بهم من يردى

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p80#3/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p80#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p80#3/r1.claim: Aladd al-khiṣām means the fiercest in disputation; a man can be called aladd and a people lud.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p80#3/r1.anchor: {ألد الخصام} أشدهم خصومة. يقال: رجل ألد، بين اللدد. وقوم لد.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p80#3/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p80#3/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p80#3/r2.claim: Khiṣām is a plural of khaṣm and has the plural forms fuʿūl and fiʿāl; khaṣm, khiṣām, and khuṣūm are cited.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p80#3/r2.anchor: والخصام جمع خصم. ويجمع على فعول وفعال. يقال: خصم وخصام وخصوم.

NAHHAS:v1p297/r9.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p297/r9.speaker: الحسن
NAHHAS:v1p297/r9.claim: Al-Ḥasan identifies the person whose speech impresses as a liar; other reported identifications are a wrongdoer or a hypocrite.
NAHHAS:v1p297/r9.anchor: وقال الحسن الكاذب وقيل الظالم وقيل المنافق

NAHHAS:v1p297/r10.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p297/r10.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p297/r10.claim: One reported analysis takes min here as particularized; other authorities identify the person as a wrongdoer or hypocrite.
NAHHAS:v1p297/r10.anchor: قيل من ههنا مخصوص وقال الحسن الكاذب وقيل الظالم وقيل المنافق

NAHHAS:v1p297/r11.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p297/r11.speaker: ابن محيصن
NAHHAS:v1p297/r11.claim: Ibn Muḥayṣin reads yashhadu with fatḥ on yāʾ and hāʾ, rather than the causative form.
NAHHAS:v1p297/r11.anchor: وقرأ ابن محيصن ( ويشهد الله على ما في قلبه ) بفتح الياء والهاء

NAHHAS:v1p297/r12.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p297/r12.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p297/r12.claim: Aladd follows the pattern of ladidtu aluddu; Abū Isḥāq takes khiṣām as a plural of khaṣm, while another view makes it the verbal noun of khāṣama.
NAHHAS:v1p297/r12.anchor: ( وهو ألد الخصام ) الفعل مثل منه لددت تلد وعلى قول أبي إسحاق خصام جمع خصم

SAMIN-DURR:2:204/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:204/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:204/r1.claim: Man may be a relative pronoun or an indefinite noun qualified by the following clause, as in a parallel earlier in the sūra.
SAMIN-DURR:2:204/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى: { من يعجبك }: " من " يجوز أن تكون موصولة، وأن تكون نكرة موصوفة،

SAMIN-DURR:2:204/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:204/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:204/r2.claim: Iʿjāb is finding something pleasing, inclining toward it, and esteeming it; the hamza makes the verb transitive.
SAMIN-DURR:2:204/r2.anchor: والإعجاب: استحسان الشيء والميل إليه والتعظيم له. والهمزة فيه للتعدي.

SAMIN-DURR:2:204/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:204/r3.speaker: الراغب
SAMIN-DURR:2:204/r3.claim: Al-Rāghib defines wonder as perplexity caused by ignorance of a thing's cause, relational rather than an intrinsic quality; a thing that amazes me appears in a way whose cause I do not know.
SAMIN-DURR:2:204/r3.anchor: وقال الراغب: " العجب حيرة تعرض للإنسان

SAMIN-DURR:2:204/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:204/r4.speaker: الشاعر
SAMIN-DURR:2:204/r4.claim: An unattributed poem uses ʿajibtu for wondering at a goat that insulted the speaker, though he had not struck it.
SAMIN-DURR:2:204/r4.anchor: ويقال: عجبت من كذا، قال: 893 عجبت والدهر كثير عجبه

SAMIN-DURR:2:204/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:204/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:204/r5.claim: Fī al-ḥayāt may modify qawlihi: he impresses the listener with claims about worldly affairs because he seeks worldly advantage through false professions of love.
SAMIN-DURR:2:204/r5.anchor: أحدهما أن يتعلق ب " قوله " ، أي: يعجبك ما يقوله في معنى الدنيا، لأن ادعاءه

SAMIN-DURR:2:204/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:204/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:204/r6.claim: Alternatively, fī al-ḥayāt modifies yuʿjibuka: his speech is pleasing and eloquent in worldly life, but not in the afterlife because of speech difficulty there or because he is not allowed to speak.
SAMIN-DURR:2:204/r6.anchor: والثاني: أن يتعلق ب " يعجبك " أي: قوله حلو فصيح في الدنيا

SAMIN-DURR:2:204/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:204/r7.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:2:204/r7.claim: The shaykh prefers attachment to yuʿjibuka, meaning the man speaks pleasing, polished words throughout his life and never switches to harsh speech; he rejects al-Zamakhsharī's construal.
SAMIN-DURR:2:204/r7.anchor: قال الشيخ: " والذي يظهر أنه متعلق بيعجبك، لا على المعنى الذي قاله الزمخشري، بل

SAMIN-DURR:2:204#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:204#2/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:204#2/r1.claim: The clause may coordinate with yuʿjibuka; it is then a relative clause without syntactic position, or an adjective in the nominative if man is indefinite.
SAMIN-DURR:2:204#2/r1.anchor: أظهرهما: أنها عطف على " يعجبك " ، فهي صلة لا محل لها من الإعراب أو صفة،

SAMIN-DURR:2:204#2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:204#2/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:204#2/r2.claim: Alternatively, the clause is circumstantial, attached either to the concealed subject of yuʿjibuka or to the genitive pronoun in qawlihi; this restricts the admiration and speech unnaturally, and a positive imperfect seldom serves as a circumstantial clause without an implied huwa.
SAMIN-DURR:2:204#2/r2.anchor: والثاني: أن تكون حالية، وفي صاحبها حينئذ وجهان، أحدهما: أنه الضمير المرفوع المستكن

SAMIN-DURR:2:204#2/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:204#2/r3.speaker: الجمهور
SAMIN-DURR:2:204#2/r3.claim: The majority read yushhidu in the active, with ḍamma on the prefix and kasra on hāʾ, taking Allah as its object.
SAMIN-DURR:2:204#2/r3.anchor: والجمهور على ضم حرف المضارعة وكسر الهاء، مأخوذا من أشهد ونصب الجلالة مفعولا به.

SAMIN-DURR:2:204#2/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:204#2/r4.speaker: أبو حيوة وابن محيصن
SAMIN-DURR:2:204#2/r4.claim: Abū Ḥaywa and Ibn Muḥayṣin read with fatḥa on both letters, making Allah the subject.
SAMIN-DURR:2:204#2/r4.anchor: وقرأ أبو حيوة وابن محيصن بفتحهما ورفع الجلالة فاعلا

SAMIN-DURR:2:204#2/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:204#2/r5.speaker: أبي
SAMIN-DURR:2:204#2/r5.claim: Ubayy reads yastashhidu Allāh; istifʿāl can mean ifʿāl and match the majority reading, or it can mean the bare verb شهد with Allah as object after an omitted preposition.
SAMIN-DURR:2:204#2/r5.anchor: وأما قراءة أبي فيحتمل استفعل وجهين، أحدهما: أن يكون بمعنى أفعل

SAMIN-DURR:2:204#2/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:204#2/r6.speaker: الجمهور
SAMIN-DURR:2:204#2/r6.claim: The majority explanation takes the phrase as swearing by God and calling Him witness that the speaker is truthful; the author says the actual sense is that God knows the concealed contents of his heart.
SAMIN-DURR:2:204#2/r6.anchor: يحلف بالله ويشهده إنه صادق، وقد جاءت الشهادة بمعنى القسم

SAMIN-DURR:2:204#2/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:204#2/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:204#2/r7.claim: The author rejects taking quadriliteral ashhada as an oath verb: oath usage belongs to triliteral shahida, so the mainstream reading means that God sees what is hidden in the man's heart.
SAMIN-DURR:2:204#2/r7.anchor: لأن المستعمل بمعنى القسم " شهد " الثلاثي لا " أشهد " الرباعي،

SAMIN-DURR:2:204#2/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:204#2/r8.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:204#2/r8.claim: To make the reported oath interpretation fit, an omitted phrase must say that he swears against his heart: what he privately holds is disbelief, so he swears to its opposite, the pleasing claim he presents.
SAMIN-DURR:2:204#2/r8.anchor: تقديره: ويحلف بالله على خلاف ما في قلبه، لأن الذي في قلبه هو الكفر،

SAMIN-DURR:2:204#2/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:204#2/r9.speaker: أبو حيوة
SAMIN-DURR:2:204#2/r9.claim: Abū Ḥaywa's reading supports the sense that God sees the disbelief concealed in the man's heart.
SAMIN-DURR:2:204#2/r9.anchor: ويقوي هذا التأويل قراءة أبي حيوة؛ إذ معناها: ويطلع الله على ما في قلبه من الكفر.

SAMIN-DURR:2:204#3/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:204#3/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:204#3/r1.claim: The syntax of wa-huwa aladdu al-khiṣām follows the alternatives given for the preceding clause, and it may additionally be circumstantial from the pronoun in yushhidu.
SAMIN-DURR:2:204#3/r1.anchor: الكلام في هذه الجملة كالتي قبلها، ونزيد عليها وجها آخر وهو أن تكون حالا من الضمير

SAMIN-DURR:2:204#3/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:204#3/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:204#3/r2.claim: Al-add means fiercely contentious, from lidad, intense disputation; an unattributed poem uses alad for a fierce opponent.
SAMIN-DURR:2:204#3/r2.anchor: والألد: الشديد من اللدد وهو شدة الخصومة، قال: 895 إن تحت التراب عزما وحزما

SAMIN-DURR:2:204#3/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:204#3/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:204#3/r3.claim: The author gives lidad verb patterns for prevailing in disputation; an unattributed line uses talid for outdoing stubborn opponents.
SAMIN-DURR:2:204#3/r3.anchor: ويقال: لددت بكسر العين ألد بفتحها، ولددته بفتح العين ألد بضمها أي: غلبته

SAMIN-DURR:2:204#3/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:204#3/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:204#3/r4.claim: A man may be called alad, alandad, or yalandad; the feminine is ladda and the plural is lud, like ḥumur.
SAMIN-DURR:2:204#3/r4.anchor: ورجل ألد وألندد ويلندد، وامرأة لداء، والجمع لد كحمر.

SAMIN-DURR:2:204#3/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:204#3/r5.speaker: الزجاج
SAMIN-DURR:2:204#3/r5.claim: Al-Zajjāj derives alad from the two lidadī of the neck, its sides.
SAMIN-DURR:2:204#3/r5.anchor: وفي اشتقاقه أقوال، أحدها: من لديدي العنق وهما صفحتاه قاله الزجاج،

SAMIN-DURR:2:204#3/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:204#3/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:204#3/r6.claim: Another derivation is from the two sides of a valley, also called lidadī because they curve.
SAMIN-DURR:2:204#3/r6.anchor: وقيل: من لديدي الوادي وهما جانباه، سميا بذلك لاعوجاجهما

SAMIN-DURR:2:204#3/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:204#3/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:204#3/r7.claim: A third derivation connects the word with ladda, to confine: the disputant holds his opponent back from conducting the argument.
SAMIN-DURR:2:204#3/r7.anchor: وقيل: هو من لده إذا حبسه فكأنه يحبس خصمه عن مفاوضته.

SAMIN-DURR:2:204#3/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:204#3/r8.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:204#3/r8.claim: One parse treats al-khiṣām as the plural of khaṣm, like kaʿb/kiʿāb, so no adjustment is needed for the predicate.
SAMIN-DURR:2:204#3/r8.anchor: وفي " الخصام " قولان، أحدهما: أنه جمع خصم/ بالفتح نحو: كعب وكعاب

SAMIN-DURR:2:204#3/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:204#3/r9.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:204#3/r9.claim: If al-khiṣām is a verbal noun, the predicate needs an interpretation: omit a first complement (his quarrel is the fiercest), a second complement (fiercest among disputants), or use the verbal noun as an agent adjective.
SAMIN-DURR:2:204#3/r9.anchor: والثاني: أنه مصدر، يقال: خاصم خصاما نحو: قاتل قتالا، وعلى هذا فلا بد من مصحح

SAMIN-DURR:2:204#3/r10.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:204#3/r10.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:204#3/r10.claim: A further proposal takes afʿal as noncomparative, meaning ladhīd al-khiṣām, and analyzes the phrase as an adjective annexed to its complement.
SAMIN-DURR:2:204#3/r10.anchor: ليست للتفضيل، بل هي بمعنى لديد الخصام، فهو من باب إضافة الصفة المشبهة.

SAMIN-DURR:2:204#3/r11.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:204#3/r11.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:2:204#3/r11.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī says al-khiṣām means disputation and the annexation of al-add has the sense of fī, like thabata al-ghadr.
SAMIN-DURR:2:204#3/r11.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: " والخصام المخاصمة، وإضافة الألد بمعنى " في " كقولهم:

SAMIN-DURR:2:204#3/r12.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:204#3/r12.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:2:204#3/r12.claim: The shaykh rejects al-Zamakhsharī's fī-genitive analysis as contrary to the usual rule that afʿal is annexed to something of which it is a part, and notes that annexation meaning fī is weak.
SAMIN-DURR:2:204#3/r12.anchor: قال الشيخ: " وهذا مخالف لما يزعمه النحاة من أن أفعل لا تضاف إلا إلى ما هي بعضه،

SAMIN-DURR:2:204#3/r13.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:204#3/r13.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:204#3/r13.claim: One proposal takes huwa not as the pronoun of man, but as referring to the quarrel: his quarrel is the fiercest quarrel.
SAMIN-DURR:2:204#3/r13.anchor: وقيل: " هو " ليس ضمير " من " بل ضمير الخصومة يفسره سياق الكلام،

SAMIN-DURR:2:204#3/r14.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:204#3/r14.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:2:204#3/r14.claim: Abū al-Baqāʾ takes huwa as referring to the verbal source qawlihi, which is construed as khuṣām.
SAMIN-DURR:2:204#3/r14.anchor: وجعل أبو البقاء " هو " ضمير المصدر الذي هو " قوله " فإنه قال:

ZAJJAJ:v1p276/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p276/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p276/r4.claim: Man is nominative under either of two parses: as the initial subject or through the governing factor in min.
ZAJJAJ:v1p276/r4.anchor: موضع (من) رفع على ضربين: على الابتداء، وبالعامل في (من)

ZAJJAJ:v1p276/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p276/r5.speaker: رجل من ثقيف
ZAJJAJ:v1p276/r5.claim: A report says a man from Thaqīf impressed the Prophet with his speech while inwardly concealing the opposite of his attractive outward presentation.
ZAJJAJ:v1p276/r5.anchor: ويروى أن رجلا من ثقيف كان يعجب النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - كلامه

ZAJJAJ:v1p276/r6.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p276/r6.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p276/r6.claim: If the form yashhadu Allāh is read, it is valid and means God knows what the hypocrite keeps secret, thereby informing the Prophet of his true condition.
ZAJJAJ:v1p276/r6.anchor: وإن قلت ويشهد الله على ما في قلبه فهو جائز إن كان قد قرئ به

ZAJJAJ:v1p276/r7.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p276/r7.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p276/r7.claim: Aladd al-khiṣām means fierce in disputation; its derivation is from the two sides of the neck, since he prevails whichever direction an argument takes.
ZAJJAJ:v1p276/r7.anchor: ومعنى خصم ألد في اللغة - الشديد الخصومة والجدل، واشتقاقه من لديدي العنق

ZAJJAJ:v1p276/r8.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p276/r8.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p276/r8.claim: The forms are aladd for a man, ladāʾ for a woman, and ladd for a group; lidadtu fulānan means I argued with and defeated him.
ZAJJAJ:v1p276/r8.anchor: يقال رجل ألد، وامرأة لداء وقوم لد - وقد لددت فلانا ألده

ZAJJAJ:v1p276/r9.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p276/r9.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p276/r9.claim: Khiṣām can pluralize khiṣm as an adjective, alongside khuṣūm; when khiṣm is a noun, fiʿāl is the larger plural, as in farakh, afrākh, firākh, and furūkh.
ZAJJAJ:v1p276/r9.anchor: وخصام جمع خصم، لأن فعلا يجمع إذا كان صفة على فعال، نحو صعب وصعاب

ASAD-NOTES:2:204#n187/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:2:204#n187/r1.speaker: Asad
ASAD-NOTES:2:204#n187/r1.claim: Asad rejects the suggestion that this describes a particular contemporary of the Prophet, finding no valid reason for that identification.
ASAD-NOTES:2:204#n187/r1.anchor: no valid reason to suppose, as some commentators do, that this refers to a particular person

ASAD-NOTES:2:204#n187/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:2:204#n187/r2.speaker: Asad
ASAD-NOTES:2:204#n187/r2.claim: He takes the passage generally, following the most reliable authorities, as contrasting people focused only on worldly life with those mindful of the hereafter too.
ASAD-NOTES:2:204#n187/r2.anchor: the most reliable authorities hold that the above passage has a general meaning

ASAD-NOTES:2:204#n187/r3.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:2:204#n187/r3.speaker: Asad
ASAD-NOTES:2:204#n187/r3.claim: The context makes this a further elaboration of the contrast between two attitudes introduced in 2:200–201.
ASAD-NOTES:2:204#n187/r3.anchor: it is a further elaboration of the allusion, made in 2:200-201, to two contrasting attitudes

ASAD-NOTES:2:204#n188/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:2:204#n188/r1.speaker: Az-Zajjaj
ASAD-NOTES:2:204#n188/r1.claim: Az-Zajjaj, as quoted by Razi, explains the phrase as someone adept at defeating opponents in controversy with extremely adroit, often misleading arguments.
ASAD-NOTES:2:204#n188/r1.anchor: According to Az-Zajjaj (quoted by Razi), this signifies a person who is always able to defeat his opponent

ASAD-NOTES:2:204#n188/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:2:204#n188/r2.speaker: Asad
ASAD-NOTES:2:204#n188/r2.claim: Asad sees people with plausible social-improvement aims who exclude the hereafter and use apparently sound ethical arguments to justify exclusive concern with worldly affairs.
ASAD-NOTES:2:204#n188/r2.anchor: people who hold plausible and even admirable views regarding a possible improvement of human society

ASAD-NOTES:2:204#n188/r3.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:2:204#n188/r3.speaker: Asad
ASAD-NOTES:2:204#n188/r3.claim: Asad says this mindset has an inescapable affinity with the attitude described in 2:8–12.
ASAD-NOTES:2:204#n188/r3.anchor: There is an inescapable affinity between the mental attitude described in the above passage and the one spoken of in 2:8-12

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p528/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p528/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p528/r1.claim: The transmitted gloss explains aladd al-khiṣām as a disputant who argues falsely; a verse by Muhalhil is cited as evidence.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p528/r1.anchor: فقال: الجدِل المخاصِم في الباطل. واستشهد بقول مهلهل:

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p528/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p528/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p528/r2.claim: The author links the singular aladd with the plural lud in Maryam, where the Prophet is told to warn a contentious people.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p528/r2.anchor: ومعها آية مريم 97: خطاباً للنبي عليه الصلاة والسلام

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p528/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p528/r3.speaker: الفراء
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p528/r3.claim: Al-Farrāʾ gives aladd as masculine, ludd as plural, and laddāʾ as feminine; to lad someone is to overcome him in dispute.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p528/r3.anchor: قال الفراء: يقال للرجل هو ألد من قوم لد، والمرأة لداء ونسوة لد. إذا غلبت الرجل في الخصومة فقد لددته

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p528/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p528/r4.speaker: أبو عبيدة
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p528/r4.claim: Abū ʿUbayda defines aladd as fiercely contentious, notes its use for a sinner, and gives ladad as its verbal noun.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p528/r4.anchor: قال أبو عبيدة: الألد شديد الخصومة، ويقال للفاجر:

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p528/r5.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p528/r5.speaker: النبي
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p528/r5.claim: ʿĀʾisha reports the Prophet saying that the most hateful man to God is the obstinate litigant.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p528/r5.anchor: حديث عائشة - رضي الله عنها -: قال رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم -:

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p528/r6.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p528/r6.speaker: ابن حجر
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p528/r6.claim: Ibn Ḥajar parses aladd as a comparative form from ladad, denoting intense contentiousness.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p528/r6.anchor: قال في فتح الباري: ألد، أفعل تفضيل من اللدد، شدة الخصومة.

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p529/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p529/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p529/r1.claim: Some take aladd as a verbal noun or as an active sense meaning “intense in dispute,” rather than as a comparative.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p529/r1.anchor: ويحتمل أن يكون مصدراً. وقيل: أفعل هنا ليست للتفضيل بل بمعنى الفاعل

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p529/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p529/r2.speaker: الراغب
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p529/r2.claim: Al-Rāghib defines aladd as a contentious opponent stubbornly defending his proof and cites the plural lud in Maryam.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p529/r2.anchor: والألد. عند الراغب، الخصيم الشديد التأبي لحجته وجمعه لد

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p529/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p529/r3.speaker: ابن الأثير
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p529/r3.claim: Ibn al-Athīr interprets the Prophetic description as meaning intensely contentious.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p529/r3.anchor: وفسره ابن الأثير في حديث عائشة - رضي الله عنها - ترفعه

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p529/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p529/r4.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p529/r4.claim: Lexicons connect the root with the two sides of a valley or neck, turning side to side, and medicine poured into one side of the mouth; ladad denotes stubborn dispute.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p529/r4.anchor: اللديدان جانبا الوادي وصفحتا العنق، ومنه اشتقاق التلدد، أي الالتفاف يميناً وشمالاً.

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p529/r5.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p529/r5.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p529/r5.claim: From the verse’s context, the author reads aladd al-khiṣām as a disputant who argues falsely.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p529/r5.anchor: وتأويلها في المسألة بالجدل المخاصم في الباطل، مستفاد من سياق الآية

NASHR:v1p51#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p51#2/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
