NASHR:v1p51#2/r1.claim: In reports about two differing reciters, the Prophet praises each with formulas such as “well done,” “correct,” and “thus it was revealed,” affirming both readings.
NASHR:v1p51#2/r1.anchor: وإلى ذلك أشار النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - حيث قال: لأحد المختلفين: " أحسنت "

NASHR:v1p51#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p51#2/r2.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p51#2/r2.claim: Unlike juristic disagreement, where one position is true in itself and another may err, every variant reading is true, correct, and from God.
NASHR:v1p51#2/r2.anchor: وبهذا افترق اختلاف القراء من اختلاف الفقهاء، فإن اختلاف القراء كل حق وصواب نزل من عند الله

NASHR:v1p51#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p51#2/r3.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p51#2/r3.claim: Attributing a reading to a Companion means that person was especially precise, frequent, or committed in reciting and teaching it, not that they originated it.
NASHR:v1p51#2/r3.anchor: إنما هو من حيث إنه كان أضبط له وأكثر قراءة وإقراء به، وملازمة له، وميلا إليه

NASHR:v1p51#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p51#2/r4.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p51#2/r4.claim: Attribution to a reading imam or transmitter denotes selecting, favoring, and consistently teaching a linguistic form until it became associated with that reader; it does not denote invention or personal derivation.
NASHR:v1p51#2/r4.anchor: إضافة اختيار ودوام ولزوم لا إضافة اختراع ورأي واجتهاد

NASHR:v1p51#2/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p51#2/r5.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p51#2/r5.claim: The variations also ease recitation and lessen the burden on the community.
NASHR:v1p51#2/r5.anchor: غير ما قدمناه من سبب التهوين والتسهيل والتخفيف على الأمة

NASHR:v1p51#2/r6.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p51#2/r6.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p51#2/r6.claim: Their variation reaches the highest eloquence and brevity: each reading can function like a verse, avoiding the length that separate verses for every wording would require.
NASHR:v1p51#2/r6.anchor: إذ كل قراءة بمنزلة الآية، إذ كان تنوع اللفظ بكلمة تقوم مقام آيات

NASHR:v1p51#2/r7.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p51#2/r7.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p51#2/r7.claim: Despite their variety, the readings do not contradict one another; they confirm and explain one another, proving the truth of the Prophet who brought them.
NASHR:v1p51#2/r7.anchor: لم يتطرق إليه تضاد ولا تناقض ولا تخالف، بل كله يصدق بعضه بعضا، ويبين بعضه بعضا

NASHR:v2p464/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p464/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
NASHR:v2p464/r1.claim: A report attributed to the Prophet gives a prayer at completion of the Qurʾan asking for mercy, guidance, remembrance, knowledge, nightly and daytime recitation, and the Qurʾan as proof.
NASHR:v2p464/r1.anchor: كان رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم -: يقول عند ختم القرآن " اللهم ارحمني بالقرآن

NASHR:v2p464/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p464/r2.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p464/r2.claim: Ibn al-Jazarī grades the completion prayer report muʿḍal because its narrator Dāwūd ibn Qays was from the tābiʿ al-tābiʿīn; he says he knows no other Prophetic report on completing the Qurʾan.
NASHR:v2p464/r2.anchor: حديث معضل لأن داود بن قيس هذا هو الفراء الدباغ المدني من تابعي التابعين

NASHR:v2p464/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p464/r3.speaker: أبو هريرة
NASHR:v2p464/r3.claim: Ibn al-Jawzī reports from Abū Hurayra that the Prophet prayed standing when finishing the Qurʾan; Ibn al-Jazarī grades it weak because its chain includes al-Ḥārith ibn Shurayḥ, criticized by hadith critics.
NASHR:v2p464/r3.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال: كان رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - إذا ختم القرآن دعا قائما كذا رواه أبو الفرج بن الجوزي في كتابه الوفا، وهو حديث ضعيف

QIRAAT-ER:2:204:18#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:2:204:18#1/r1.speaker: skn
QIRAAT-ER:2:204:18#1/r1.claim: Sukūn on hāʾ compresses wa-huwa to wa-hwa in rapid recitation without changing meaning.
QIRAAT-ER:2:204:18#1/r1.anchor: Sukūn on hāʾ: wa-hwa instead of wa-huwa — phonetic compression in rapid recitation; no semantic change

IBNHISHAM:v2p174/r1.author: Ibn Hishām
IBNHISHAM:v2p174/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNHISHAM:v2p174/r1.claim: In year three, after the al-Raji' detachment including Murthid and Asim was killed, hypocrites mocked them; Ibn Abbas says the verse was revealed about their words and the dead men's reward.
IBNHISHAM:v2p174/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس: لما أصيبت السرية التي كان فيها مرثد وعاصم بالرجيع، قال رجال من المنافقين

IBNHISHAM:v2p174/r2.author: Ibn Hishām
IBNHISHAM:v2p174/r2.speaker: ابن إسحاق
IBNHISHAM:v2p174/r2.claim: The hypocrite displays Islam with his tongue while his heart contradicts his speech.
IBNHISHAM:v2p174/r2.anchor: أي لما يظهر من الإسلام بلسانه، «ويشهد الله على ما في قلبه» 2: 204، وهو مخالف لما يقول بلسانه

IBNHISHAM:v2p174/r3.author: Ibn Hishām
IBNHISHAM:v2p174/r3.speaker: ابن إسحاق
IBNHISHAM:v2p174/r3.claim: The phrase describes someone given to argument whenever addressed and answered.
IBNHISHAM:v2p174/r3.anchor: «وهو ألد الخصام» 2: 204: أي ذو جدال إذا كلمك وراجعك

IBNHISHAM:v2p174#2/r1.author: Ibn Hishām
IBNHISHAM:v2p174#2/r1.speaker: ابن هشام
IBNHISHAM:v2p174#2/r1.claim: Al-add is a person who stirs up conflict, intensifying the quarrel; its plural is lud. Ibn Hisham cites Qur'an 19:97 and Mahllal's poem, which has a transmitted variant for the final word.
IBNHISHAM:v2p174#2/r1.anchor: قال ابن هشام: الألد: الذي يشغب، فتشتد خصومته، وجمعه: لد

IBNHISHAM:v2p174#2/r2.author: Ibn Hishām
IBNHISHAM:v2p174#2/r2.speaker: الطرماح بن حكيم الطائي
IBNHISHAM:v2p174#2/r2.claim: Al-Tirmah calls the chameleon an obstinate opponent, using al-andad as a poetic form related to al-add.
IBNHISHAM:v2p174#2/r2.anchor: قال الطرماح بن حكيم الطائي يصف الحرباء: يوفي على جذم الجذول كأنه ... خصم أبر على الخصوم ألندد

ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p81/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p81/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p81/r1.claim: Qatāda identifies the person whose speech impresses as a hypocrite.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p81/r1.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ ومن الناس من يعجبك قوله في الحياة الدنيا ويشهد الله على ما في قلبه ﴾ قال هو المنافق

ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p81/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p81/r2.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p81/r2.claim: Qatāda explains “most contentious” as arguing by means of falsehood.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p81/r2.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ وهو ألد الخصام ﴾ قال جدل بالباطل

ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p81#2/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p81#2/r1.speaker: عائشة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p81#2/r1.claim: ʿĀʾisha reports that the most detested kind of man to the Messenger of God was the stubborn, contentious opponent.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p81#2/r1.anchor: عن عائشة قالت كان أبغض الرجال إلى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم الألد الخصم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p315/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p315/r6.speaker: المفضل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p315/r6.claim: Al-Mufaddal says the root idea of wonder is encountering something unlike anything else.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p315/r6.anchor: وأصله، لما لم يكن مثله قاله المفضل،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p315/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p315/r7.speaker: الراغب
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p315/r7.claim: Al-Raghib describes wonder as perplexity arising from something whose cause the observer does not know.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p315/r7.anchor: وقال الراغب: العجب حيرة تعرض للإنسان بسبب الشيء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p315/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p315/r8.speaker: الراغب
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p315/r8.claim: Al-Raghib says wonder depends on the observer’s knowledge rather than being an intrinsic property of the thing.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p315/r8.anchor: بل هو بحسب الإضافات إلى من يعرف السبب، ومن لا يعرفه.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p315/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p315/r9.speaker: الراغب
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p315/r9.claim: Al-Raghib says “this amazed me” means it appeared in a way whose cause I did not know.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p315/r9.anchor: وحقيقة أعجبني كذا أي: ظهر لي ظهورا لم أعرف سببه.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p315/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p315/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p315/r10.claim: The expression “I wondered at this” can signal reproach, as in a line by Ziyad al-Aʿjam.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p315/r10.anchor: وقد يقال عجبت من كذا في الإنكار، كما قال زياد الأعجم:

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p316/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p316/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p316/r1.claim: Ladad means intense disputation; the source gives its verb and adjective forms and says one who overcomes an opponent “laddahu.”
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p316/r1.anchor: ورجل ألد وامرأة لداء، ورجال ونساء لد،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p316/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p316/r2.speaker: الزجاج
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p316/r2.claim: Al-Zajjaj derives lidad from the two sides of the neck.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p316/r2.anchor: واشتقاقه من لديدي العنق، وهما: صفحتاه، قاله الزجاج،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p316/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p316/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p316/r3.claim: Alternative derivations are the crooked sides of a valley or ladda, “he restrained him,” because a fierce disputant holds his opponent back from argument.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p316/r3.anchor: وقيل: من لديدي الوادي وهما جانباه، سميا بذلك لاعوجاجهما،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p316/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p316/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p316/r4.claim: A further derivation links the word to restraining someone, because a fierce disputant blocks his opponent’s argument.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p316/r4.anchor: وقيل: هو من لده: حبسه، فكأنه يحبس خصمه عن مفاوضته

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p316/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p316/r5.speaker: الراجز
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p316/r5.claim: A rajaz line uses ladad for a fierce opponent who overcomes his peers.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p316/r5.anchor: وقال الراجز: يلد أقران الرجال اللدد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p316/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p316/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p316/r6.claim: Khiṣām is the verbal noun of arguing and can be a plural of khaṣm, with forms khaṣm, khuṣūm, and khiṣām.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p316/r6.anchor: الخصام: مصدر خاصم، وجمع خصم يقال: خصم وخصوم وخصام،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p316/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p316/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p316/r7.claim: The underlying sense of disputation is probing deeply into a matter; container corners are also called khuṣūm, singular khaṣm.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p316/r7.anchor: والأصل في الخصومة التعميق في البحث عن الشيء، ولذلك قيل: في زوايا الأوعية: خصوم،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p316/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p316/r13.speaker: زياد الأعجم
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p316/r13.claim: Ziyad al-Aʿjam’s poem uses wonder reproachfully: he marvels that a man insulted him and he did not hit him.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p316/r13.anchor: عجبت والدهر كثير عجبه ... من عنزي سبني لم أضربه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p324/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p324/r6.speaker: عطاء والكلبي ومقاتل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p324/r6.claim: A reported occasion identifies al-Akhnas ibn Shariq, also called Ubayy, as a smooth-tongued, attractive man who professed love and Islam to the Prophet, concealed his intent, then burned Thaqif's crops and killed their livestock after a dispute.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p324/r6.anchor: نزلت في الأخنس بن شريق واسمه: أبي، وكان حلو اللسان والمنظر، يجالس رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم، ويظهر حبه، والإسلام، ويحلف على ذلك،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p324/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p324/r7.speaker: السدي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p324/r7.claim: Al-Suddi's version says al-Akhnas passed Muslim crops and donkeys, burned the crops, and spared the donkeys.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p324/r7.anchor: وقال السدي: فمر بزرع للمسلمين وحمر، فأحرق الزرع، وغفر الحمر،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p324/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p324/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p324/r8.claim: It is also said that this verse refers to the people described as a slanderous swearer in 68:10 and a backbiter in 104:1.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p324/r8.anchor: قيل: وفيه نزلت ولا تطع كل حلاف مهين وويل لكل همزة لمزة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p325/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p325/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p325/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that Quraysh unbelievers deceitfully claimed conversion and asked for teachers; the Prophet sent Khubayb, Murshid, Asim ibn Thabit, Ibn al-Duthanna, and others in the Rajīʿ expedition, where they were killed. Rajīʿ lies between Mecca and Medina; the account is well known in the canonical collections.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p325/r1.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: في كفار قريش، أرسلوا إلى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: إنا قد أسلمنا، فابعث إلينا من يعلمنا دينك، وكان ذلك مكرا منهم،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p325/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p325/r2.speaker: قتادة وابن زيد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p325/r2.claim: Qatada and Ibn Zayd say the verse addresses every hypocrite whose tongue says what the heart does not contain.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p325/r2.anchor: وقال قتادة، وابن زيد: نزلت في كل منافق أظهر بلسانه ما ليس في قلبه.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p325/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p325/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p325/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that hypocrites mocked the Rajīʿ expedition, asking what the men had lost at home and saying they had not delivered their companion's message.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p325/r3.anchor: وروي عن ابن عباس: أنها في المنافقين، قالوا عن سرية الرجيع: ويح هؤلاء ما فقدوا في بيوتهم، ولا أدوا رسالة صاحبهم.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p325/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p325/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p325/r4.claim: Following the two kinds of supplicants in 2:200–201, the passage contrasts a sweet-speaking worldly seeker with one who seeks God's pleasure and gives himself for it; the first comes first as in the earlier division. Outer speech should match inner belief.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p325/r4.anchor: ومناسبة هذه الآية لما قبلها هو أنه: لما قسم السائلين الله قبل إلى: مقتصر على أمر الدنيا، وسائل حسنة الدنيا والآخرة، والوقاية من النار،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p325/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p325/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p325/r5.claim: من in من يعجبك may be a relative pronoun or an indefinite noun described by the following clause.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p325/r5.anchor: من، من قوله: من يعجبك، موصولة، وقيل: نكرة موصوفة،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p325/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p325/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p325/r6.claim: The address in يعجبك is to the Prophet if the verse concerns a named person, or to any believer if its subject is the general class of hypocrites.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p325/r6.anchor: يعجبك، خطاب للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم إن كانت نزلت في معين، كالأخنس أو غيره،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p325/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p325/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p325/r7.claim: His speech impresses because it appears to accord with the addressee's faith and goodness.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p325/r7.anchor: ومعنى إعجاب قوله استحسانه لموافقة ما أنت عليه من الإيمان والخير،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p325/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p325/r8.speaker: الترمذي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p325/r8.claim: A report cited in al-Tirmidhi says that some servants of God have tongues sweeter than honey and hearts more bitter than colocynth; no grading is stated.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p325/r8.anchor: وجاء في الترمذي: «أن في بعض كتب الله إن من عباد الله قوما ألسنتهم من العسل، وقلوبهم أمر من الصبر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p326/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p326/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p326/r1.claim: One parses في الحياة as attached to قوله: the false claim of love and allegiance seeks worldly gain, while the afterlife requires true faith and sincere love.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p326/r1.anchor: في الحياة: متعلق بقوله، أي يعجبك مقالته في معنى الدنيا، لأن ادعاءه المحبة والتبعية بالباطل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p326/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p326/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p326/r2.claim: Al-Zamakhshari allows attachment to يعجبك, so the speech impresses in worldly life but not at resurrection when he is held back or barred from speaking; Abu Hayyan calls this remote.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p326/r2.anchor: وقال الزمخشري، بعد أن ذكر هذا الوجه: ويجوز أن يتعلق بيعجبك أي: قوله حلو، فيصح: في الدنيا، فهو يعجبك ولا يعجبك في الآخرة،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p326/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p326/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p326/r3.claim: Abu Hayyan prefers attachment to يعجبك: throughout his life the man's outward speech sounds graceful and appealing, even as it shifts into harsh contradiction.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p326/r3.anchor: والذي يظهر أنه متعلق بيعجبك لا على المعنى الذي قاله، والمعنى أنك تستحسن مقالته دائما في مدة حياته، إذ لا يصدر منه من القول إلا ما هو معجب رائق لطيف،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p326/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p326/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p326/r4.claim: The two descriptions concern two states: he is sweet in outward speech but fiercely contentious inwardly, while his actions contradict his attractive words.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p326/r4.anchor: إذ لا يحمل قوله: يعجبك قوله، وقوله: وهو ألد الخصام إلا على حالتين: فهو حلو المقالة في الظاهر، شديد الخصومة في الباطن.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p326/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p326/r5.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p326/r5.claim: The majority read ويشهد with yāʾ ḍamma and hāʾ kasra, and Allah accusative, from the form meaning to make God witness.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p326/r5.anchor: ويشهد الله على ما في قلبه قرأ الجمهور بضم الياء وكسر الهاء. ونصب الجلالة من: أشهد،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p326/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p326/r6.speaker: أبو حيوة وابن محيصن
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p326/r6.claim: Abu Haywa and Ibn Muhaysin read the verb with yāʾ and hāʾ open and Allah nominative, from شهد.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p326/r6.anchor: وقرأ أبو حيوة، وابن محيصن بفتح الياء والهاء ورفع الجلالة، من شهد،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p326/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p326/r7.speaker: أبي وابن مسعود
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p326/r7.claim: Ubayy and Ibn Masud read ويستشهد الله.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p326/r7.anchor: وقرأ أبي، وابن مسعود: ويستشهد الله،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p326/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p326/r8.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p326/r8.claim: The majority's usual explanation is that he swears by God that he is truthful and loves the Messenger and Islam; testimony for an oath also occurs in the mutual-imprecation passage in sura al-Nur.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p326/r8.anchor: والمعنى على قراءة الجمهور، وتفسير الجمهور، أنه يحلف بالله ويشهده أنه صادق وقائل حقا، وأنه محب في الرسول والإسلام،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p326/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p326/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p326/r9.claim: He rejects the proposal that Allah is accusative because a preposition was omitted in an oath: that omission works with the triliteral verb, not the quadriliteral form أشهد.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p326/r9.anchor: قيل: ويكون اسم الله انتصب بسقوط حرف الجر، والتقدير: ويقسم بالله على ما في قلبه، وهذا سهو، لأن الذي يكون يقسم به هو الثلاثي لا الرباعي،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p326/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p326/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p326/r10.claim: Abu Hayyan's apparent sense is that the hypocrite exposes his concealed disbelief to God alone, since what is in his heart contradicts his public claim.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p326/r10.anchor: والظاهر عندي أن المعنى: أنه يطلع الله على ما في قلبه، ولا يعلم به أحدا لشدة تكتمه وإخفائه الكفر،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p326#2/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p326#2/r1.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p326#2/r1.claim: The majority reading needs an ellipsis on the common interpretation: he swears by God to the opposite of what is in his heart, since his heart holds disbelief.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p326#2/r1.anchor: وعلى تفسير الجمهور يحتاج إلى حذف ما يصح به المعنى، أي: ويحلف بالله على خلاف ما في قلبه، لأن الذي في قلبه هو الكفر،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p326#2/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p326#2/r2.speaker: أبو حيوة وابن محيصن
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p326#2/r2.claim: Their reading supports Abu Hayyan's interpretation: God is made aware of the disbelief within, contrary to the speaker's outward words.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p326#2/r2.anchor: ويقوي هذا التأويل قراءة أبي حيوة، وابن محيصن، إذ معناها: ويطلع الله على ما في قلبه من الكفر الذي هو خلاف قوله.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p326#2/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p326#2/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p326#2/r3.claim: The reading ويستشهد can use form X in the sense of form IV, as in أيقن واستيقن, matching the majority reading.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p326#2/r3.anchor: وقراءة: ويستشهد، بجواز أن تكون فيها: استفعل، بمعنى: أفعل: نحو أيقن واستيقن،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p326#2/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p326#2/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p326#2/r4.claim: Alternatively, ويستشهد may use form X in the basic sense of شهد; Allah then requires an elided preposition, and the meaning again needs خلاف ما في قلبه to be understood.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p326#2/r4.anchor: ويجوز أن تكون فيها: استفعل، بمعنى المجرد، فيكون استشهد بمعنى شهد، ويظهر إذ ذاك أن لفظ الجلالة منصوب على إسقاط حرف الجر،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p326#2/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p326#2/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p326#2/r5.claim: The apparent syntax coordinates ويشهد الله with يعجبك, making it part of the relative clause or description; the alternative circumstantial reading would restrict the admiration or speech.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p326#2/r5.anchor: والظاهر أن قوله: ويشهد الله، معطوف على قوله: يعجبك، فهو صلة، أو صفة.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p326#2/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p326#2/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p326#2/r6.claim: A circumstantial analysis would need an implied subject, وهو, as in قمت وأصك عينه; that added ellipsis is against the default, so Abu Hayyan rejects restricting the clause as a state.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p326#2/r6.anchor: وجوز أن تكون الواو واو الحال لا واو العطف، فتكون الجملة حالا من الفاعل المستكن في: يعجبك،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p326#2/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p326#2/r7.speaker: الزجاج
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p326#2/r7.claim: Al-Zajjaj takes الخصام as the plural of خصم, so ألد الخصام means the fiercest of disputants.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p326#2/r7.anchor: أي: أشد المخاصمين، فالخصام جمع خصم، قاله الزجاج،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p326#2/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p326#2/r8.speaker: الخليل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p326#2/r8.claim: Al-Khalil takes الخصام as a verbal noun; predicating ألد of it then requires an ellipsis such as وخصامه ألد الخصام or ألد ذوي الخصام.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p326#2/r8.anchor: وإن أريد بالخصام المصدر، كما قاله الخليل، فلا بد من حذف مصحح لجريان الخبر على المبتدأ،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p326#2/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p326#2/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p326#2/r9.claim: Other grammatical possibilities treat الخصام as a verbal noun used like an active participle, take أفعل as an intensive rather than comparative, or understand the pronoun as referring to his contention itself.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p326#2/r9.anchor: وجوز أن يراد هنا بالخصام المصدر على معنى اسم الفاعل، كما يوصف بالمصدر في: رجل خصم،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p327/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p327/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p327/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses ألد الخصام as someone skilled in disputation.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p327/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس: معناه ذو الجدال،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p327/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p327/r2.speaker: الحسن
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p327/r2.claim: Al-Hasan glosses the phrase as a liar who argues falsely.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p327/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p327/r3.speaker: قتادة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p327/r3.claim: Qatada says he is fiercely obstinate in disobeying God.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p327/r3.anchor: وقال قتادة: شديد القسوة في معصية الله،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p327/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p327/r4.speaker: السدي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p327/r4.claim: Al-Suddi interprets him as crooked in disputation.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p327/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p327/r5.speaker: مجاهد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p327/r5.claim: Mujahid says he does not remain on the truth when disputing.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p327/r5.anchor: وقال مجاهد: لا يستقيم على حق في الخصومة.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p327/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p327/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p327/r6.claim: The opening nominal clause is apparently coordinated with the relative clause of من; grammarians also allow it as a circumstantial clause coordinated with ويشهد or attached to its implied subject.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p327/r6.anchor: والظاهر أن هذه الجملة الابتدائية معطوفة على صلة من، فهي صلة، وجوزوا أن تكون حالا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p327/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p327/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p327/r7.claim: The syntax of the genitive depends on whether الخصام is plural, verbal noun, active-participle sense, or an intensive adjective; each reading yields a different account of the إضافة.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p327/r7.anchor: وإذا كان الخصام جمعا، كان ألد من إضافة بعض إلى كل، وإذا كان مصدرا فقد ذكرنا تصحيح ذلك بالحذف

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p327/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p327/r8.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p327/r8.claim: Al-Zamakhshari treats الخصام as المخاصمة and the genitive as meaning في, but Abu Hayyan says this is a weak grammatical position because a superlative is normally annexed only to something it partly is.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p327/r8.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: والخصام المخاصمة، وإضافة الألد بمعنى في كقولهم ثبت الغدر. انتهى.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p327/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p327/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p327/r9.claim: The verse counsels care in religious and worldly matters and cautions judges not to rely on outward faith or righteousness without examining people's inner states.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p327/r9.anchor: قالوا: وفي هذه الآية دليل على الاحتياط بما يتعلق بأمور الدين والدنيا، واستواء أحوال الشهود والقضاة،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p358/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p358/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p358/r2.claim: The passage contrasts apparent verbal piety with inward sincerity: this person's polished, pleasing words display outward agreement and obedience, then he invokes God to swear his heart matches his speech, though he is fiercely contentious.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p358/r2.anchor: يؤنقك ويروق لفظه، يحسن ما يأتي به من الموافقة والطواعية ظاهرا، ثم لا يكتفي بما زور

ALUSI-FULL:v2p94#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p94#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p94#2/r1.claim: This continues 2:200’s division of pilgrims by their remembrance and supplication, adding hypocrites and sincere believers after the disbeliever and believer categories.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p94#2/r1.anchor: عطف على قوله تعالى : ( ومن الناس من يقول ) والجامع

ALUSI-FULL:v2p94#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p94#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p94#2/r2.claim: Taʿajjub literally involves perplexity from not knowing a cause; here it figuratively means that the eloquence and sweetness of his speech impress and magnify him, since its cause is known.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p94#2/r2.anchor: وأصل التعجب حيرة تعرض للإنسان لجهله بسبب المتعجب منه وهو هنا مجاز

ALUSI-FULL:v2p94#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p94#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p94#2/r3.claim: The phrase can mean worldly affairs and means of livelihood, whether they benefit him or not; alternatively, al-dunyā is intended because his claim professes love and faith.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p94#2/r3.anchor: فالمعنى ومنهم من يروقك ويعظم في نفسك ما يقوله : في الحياة الدنيا

ALUSI-FULL:v2p94#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p94#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p94#2/r4.claim: On the worldly-affairs reading, the phrase is a descriptive topic heading for his speech, with no ellipsis and an understood causal ظرف relation; it may instead modify يعجبك directly.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p94#2/r4.anchor: وجوز تعلق المجرور بالفعل قبله أي يعجبك في الدنيا قوله لفصاحته

ALUSI-FULL:v2p94#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p94#2/r5.speaker: السدي
ALUSI-FULL:v2p94#2/r5.claim: Al-Suddī says the verse was revealed about al-Akhnas ibn Sharīq, who professed Islam to the Prophet, then burned Muslim crops and hamstrung their donkeys.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p94#2/r5.anchor: والآية كما قال السدي : نزلت في الأخنس بن شريق الثقفي حليف بن زهرة

ALUSI-FULL:v2p94#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p94#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p94#2/r6.claim: He invokes God as witness by claiming that God knows his heart agrees with his tongue; the clause coordinates with يعجبك.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p94#2/r6.anchor: حيث يقول الله يعلم أن ما قلبي موافق لما في لساني وهو معطوف على ( يعجبك )

ALUSI-FULL:v2p94#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p94#2/r7.speaker: أبي بن كعب
ALUSI-FULL:v2p94#2/r7.claim: Ubayy’s codex reads ويستشهد الله, presenting the man as calling God to witness.

ALUSI-FULL:v2p94#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p94#2/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p94#2/r8.claim: A reading with الله in the nominative makes God the witness and takes what is in the man’s heart as its true contents.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p94#2/r8.anchor: وقريء ويشهد الله بالرفع فالمراد بما في قلبه ما فيه حقيقة

ALUSI-FULL:v2p94#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p94#2/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v2p94#2/r9.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reads والله يشهد على ما في قلبه; the clause is parenthetical, and على signals that the testimony harms the man.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p94#2/r9.anchor: ويؤيده قراءة ابن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنهما والله يشهد على ما في قلبه

ALUSI-FULL:v2p94#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p94#2/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v2p94#2/r10.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses ألد الخصام as intensely contentious in falsehood.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p94#2/r10.anchor: شديد المخاصمة في الباطل كما قال ابن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنهما

ALUSI-FULL:v2p94#2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p94#2/r11.speaker: مهلهل
ALUSI-FULL:v2p94#2/r11.claim: Alusi cites Mihlal’s verse, including خصيما, as poetic evidence in explaining the contentiousness expressed by ألد.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p94#2/r11.anchor: وأستشهد عليه بقول مهلهل : إن تحت الحجار حزما وجورا وخصيما

ALUSI-FULL:v2p94#2/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p94#2/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p94#2/r12.claim: Alusi takes ألد as an adjective like أحمر, not a comparative: it has plural لد and feminine لداء; its genitive construction links an adjective to its agent by figurative attribution.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p94#2/r12.anchor: فألد صفة كأحمر بدليل جمعه على لد ومجيء مؤنثه لداء لا أفعل تفضيل

ALUSI-FULL:v2p94#2/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p94#2/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p94#2/r13.claim: Another analysis makes the phrase mean intensely contentious in disputation, with a تقديرية ظرف relation.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p94#2/r13.anchor: أي شديد في المخاصمة ونقل أبو حيان عن الخليل أن ألد

ALUSI-FULL:v2p94#2/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p94#2/r14.speaker: أبو حيان
ALUSI-FULL:v2p94#2/r14.claim: Abū Ḥayyān transmits al-Khalīl’s view that ألد is comparative, requiring an understood الخصام ألد or ألد ذوي الخصام; other proposed referents are strained, or خصام is a plural of خصم.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p94#2/r14.anchor: ونقل أبو حيان عن الخليل أن ألد أفعل تفضيل فلا بد من تقدير

ALUSI-FULL:v2p94#2/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p94#2/r15.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p94#2/r15.claim: The verse signals that excessive quarrelsomeness is blameworthy and characteristic of hypocrites, who love worldly life and therefore dispute over it.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p94#2/r15.anchor: وفي الآية إشارة إلى أن شدة المخاصمة مذمومة

ALUSI-FULL:v2p94#2/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p94#2/r16.speaker: النبي صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم
ALUSI-FULL:v2p94#2/r16.claim: The Prophet says, as narrated by ʿĀʾisha and recorded by al-Bukhārī and Muslim, that the most hateful men to God are the obstinately disputatious.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p94#2/r16.anchor: عن عائشة رضي الله تعالى عنها عن النبي صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم أبغض الرجال

ALUSI-FULL:v2p94#2/r17.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p94#2/r17.speaker: أبو الدرداء
ALUSI-FULL:v2p94#2/r17.claim: A report from Abū al-Dardāʾ, recorded by Aḥmad, says persistent disputing makes one sinful and unjust, and persistent speaking makes one a liar, except speech concerning God.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p94#2/r17.anchor: وأخرج أحمد عن أبي الدرداء كفى بربك إثما أن لا تزال مماريا

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p235#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p235#2/r1.speaker: الكلبي ومقاتل وعطاء
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p235#2/r1.claim: Al-Kalbi, Muqatil, and Ata say the passage was revealed about al-Akhnas ibn Shariq, an ally of Banu Zuhra, also named Ubay; he withdrew from Badr with three hundred men, was charming in speech and appearance, feigned Islam and love for the Prophet, and was a hypocrite whom the Prophet drew near.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p235#2/r1.anchor: قال الكلبي ومقاتل وعطاء: نزلت في الأخنس بن شريق الثقفي

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p235#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p235#2/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p235#2/r2.claim: The speech pleases the listener and grows weighty in the heart; Arabic uses «I like this» for approval but «I am amazed at this» for dislike or disapproval.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p235#2/r2.anchor: أي تستحسنه ويعظم في قلبك، ويقال في الاستحسان أعجبني كذا

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p235#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p235#2/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p235#2/r3.claim: The hypocrite swears that he believes in the Prophet and loves him, though that claim is false.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p235#2/r3.anchor: يعني قول المنافق: والله إني بك مؤمن ولك محب

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p235#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p235#2/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p235#2/r4.claim: A person described as aladd is intensely contentious; the expression can describe someone who prevails over an opponent.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p235#2/r4.anchor: أي شديد الخصومة، يقال لددت يا هذا وأنت تلد لدا ولدادة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p235#2/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p235#2/r5.speaker: الزجاج
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p235#2/r5.claim: Al-Zajjaj derives aladd from the two sides of the neck: whichever direction the argument turns, right or left, the person prevails.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p235#2/r5.anchor: قال الزجاج: اشتقاقه من لديدي العنق وهما صفحتاه

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p235#2/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p235#2/r6.speaker: أبو عبيدة والزجاج
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p235#2/r6.claim: Abu Ubayda treats khisām as a verbal noun of disputing; al-Zajjaj also analyzes it as a plural of khasm, like baḥr and biḥār/biḥūr.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p235#2/r6.anchor: والخصام مصدر خاصمه خصاما ومخاصمة قاله أبو عبيدة: وقال الزجاج: هو جمع خصم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p235#2/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p235#2/r7.speaker: الحسن
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p235#2/r7.claim: Al-Hasan glosses the stubborn disputant as someone who lies in speech.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p235#2/r7.anchor: قال الحسن: ألد الخصام أي كاذب القول

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p235#2/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p235#2/r8.speaker: قتادة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p235#2/r8.claim: Qatada describes him as hard-hearted in disobedience, arguing falsely, speaking wisdom while acting sinfully.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p235#2/r8.anchor: قال قتادة: شديد القسوة في المعصية، جدل بالباطل يتكلم بالحكمة ويعمل بالخطيئة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p236/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p236/r1.speaker: النبي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p236/r1.claim: Aisha reports the Prophet saying that the most hateful men to God are the fiercely contentious disputants; the author gives no grading.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p236/r1.anchor: عن عائشة رضي الله عنها عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:204/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:204/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:204/r1.claim: His speech pleases you and grows impressive in your estimation; wonder is perplexity caused by ignorance of what prompted the surprise.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:204/r1.anchor: يروقك ويعظم في نفسك، والتعجب: حيرة تعرض للإنسان لجهله بسبب المتعجب منه

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:204/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:204/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:204/r2.claim: “In worldly life” may qualify what he says about worldly affairs and livelihood, or refer to the world as the object of professed love and displayed faith.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:204/r2.anchor: متعلق بالقول، أي ما يقوله في أمور الدنيا وأسباب المعاش، أو في معنى الدنيا فإنها مراد من إدعاء المحبة وإظهار الإيمان

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:204/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:204/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:204/r3.claim: Alternatively, his eloquence delights listeners in this life but not the next, when astonishment and speechlessness overtake him or he is not permitted to speak.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:204/r3.anchor: أو يعجبك أي يعجبك قوله في الدنيا حلاوة وفصاحة ولا يعجبك في الآخرة لما يعتريه من الدهشة والحبسة، أو لأنه لا يؤذن له في الكلام

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:204/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:204/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:204/r4.claim: He swears and calls God to witness that what is in his heart agrees with his speech.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:204/r4.anchor: يحلف ويستشهد الله على أن ما في قلبه موافق لكلامه

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:204/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:204/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:204/r5.claim: He is intensely hostile and argumentative toward Muslims; khisām can mean disputation or be a plural of khaṣm, making him the fiercest of disputants.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:204/r5.anchor: شديد العداوة والجدال للمسلمين، والخصام المخاصمة ويجوز أن يكون جمع خصم كصعب وصعاب بمعنى أشد الخصوم خصومة

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:204/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:204/r6.speaker: قيل
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:204/r6.claim: One reported occasion identifies the man as al-Akhnaṣ ibn Shurayq al-Thaqafī, handsome and eloquent, who professed loyalty to the Messenger and Islam.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:204/r6.anchor: قيل نزلت في الأخنس بن شريق الثقفي وكان حسن المنظر حلو المنطق يوالي رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ويدعي الإسلام

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:204/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:204/r7.speaker: قيل
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:204/r7.claim: Another reported view says the verse concerns all hypocrites.

BIQAI-FULL:v1p383#2/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p383#2/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p383#2/r1.claim: After discussing those seeking worldly benefit alone and those seeking both worlds, the passage notes the absent type rejecting both and the type seeking only the afterlife.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p383#2/r1.anchor: ولما كان قد ذكر سبحانه وتعالى الراغب في الدنيا وحدها والراغب في الدارين

BIQAI-FULL:v1p383#2/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p383#2/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p383#2/r2.claim: The dangerous case is a hypocrite who secretly seeks worldly gain while publicly presenting himself as seeking the afterlife.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p383#2/r2.anchor: إنما هو المسر لإرادة الدنيا بإظهاره لإرادة الآخرة

BIQAI-FULL:v1p383#2/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p383#2/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p383#2/r3.claim: Placed after warnings of piety and resurrection, this portrait threatens the hypocrite with resurrection and recalls the hypocrites at the sūra's opening despite the long interval.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p383#2/r3.anchor: بدأ به بعد ذكر التقوى والحشر ليكون مصدوعا بادئ بدء بذلك الأمر مقصودا بالتهديد بالحشر

BIQAI-FULL:v1p383#2/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p383#2/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p383#2/r4.claim: Min al-nās here means either a person or the person who has the described traits.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p383#2/r4.anchor: أي شخص أو الذي { يعجبك } أي يروقك

BIQAI-FULL:v1p383#2/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p383#2/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p383#2/r5.claim: Yuʿjibuka means that the person's speech pleases the listener and captures his heart; this echoes the hypocrite's deception at the sūra's beginning.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p383#2/r5.anchor: كما ذكرنا أول السورة أنه يخادع , ويعجب من الإعجاب

BIQAI-FULL:v1p383#2/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p383#2/r6.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p383#2/r6.claim: Al-Harali defines wonder as a thing's standing outside its peers, becoming rare in its kind of workmanship.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p383#2/r6.anchor: قاله الحرالي . وقال الأصبهاني : حالة تغشى الإنسان

BIQAI-FULL:v1p383#2/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p383#2/r7.speaker: الأصبهاني
BIQAI-FULL:v1p383#2/r7.claim: Al-Asbahani describes astonishment as a state covering someone who perceives excellence whose cause is unknown.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p383#2/r7.anchor: وقال الأصبهاني : حالة تغشى الإنسان عند إدراك كمال مجهول السبب

BIQAI-FULL:v1p383#2/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p383#2/r8.speaker: الراغب
BIQAI-FULL:v1p383#2/r8.claim: Al-Raghib says astonishment depends on whether the observer knows the cause; the thing appears without a known cause to that observer.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p383#2/r8.anchor: وعن الراغب أنه قال : وليس هو شيئا له في ذاته

BIQAI-FULL:v1p383#2/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p383#2/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p383#2/r9.claim: The qualification limits impressive speech to worldly life; speech in the afterlife will not be good or admirable, avoiding confusion after the preceding mention of resurrection.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p383#2/r9.anchor: ولما كان ذكر هذا بعد ذكر الحشر ربما أوهم

BIQAI-FULL:v1p383#2/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p383#2/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p383#2/r10.claim: He calls God as witness that his heart matches what he has displayed with his tongue.

BIQAI-FULL:v1p383#2/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p383#2/r11.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p383#2/r11.claim: He persists in false dispute without stopping, disguising his ugly purpose and making each argument seem attractive.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p383#2/r11.anchor: أي يتمادى في الخصام بالباطل لا ينقطع جداله كل ذلك وهو يظهر أنه على الحسن الجميل

BIQAI-FULL:v1p383#2/r12.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p383#2/r12.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p383#2/r12.claim: Al-Harali glosses lidad as the opposite of disputation, and khisām as speech entering the hearer's ear to restrain a claim.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p383#2/r12.anchor: واللدد ذدة الخصومة , والخصام القول الذي يسمع

BIQAI-FULL:v1p383#2/r13.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p383#2/r13.speaker: الأصبهاني
BIQAI-FULL:v1p383#2/r13.claim: Al-Asbahani defines khisām as excessive probing into a matter and constraining debate.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p383#2/r13.anchor: وقال الأصبهاني : هو التعمق في البحث عن الشيء والمضايقة فيه

BIQAI-FULL:v1p383#2/r14.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p383#2/r14.speaker: الأصبهاني
BIQAI-FULL:v1p383#2/r14.claim: Al-Asbahani allows khisām itself to be described as aladd by way of hyperbole.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p383#2/r14.anchor: ويجوز أن يجعل الخصام ألد على المبالغة

DURR-FULL:v1p571/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p571/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v1p571/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says the verse was revealed after hypocrites mocked the Muslims killed in the expedition that included ʿAsim and Mirthad, saying the men had neither stayed with their families nor delivered the Prophet’s message.
DURR-FULL:v1p571/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: لما أصيبت السرية

DURR-FULL:v1p571/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p571/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v1p571/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas explains that the man’s speech outwardly displays Islam, while his heart contradicts what his tongue says.
DURR-FULL:v1p571/r2.anchor: أي لما يظهر من الإسلام بلسانه

DURR-FULL:v1p571/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p571/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v1p571/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas explains the description as someone who argues fiercely and answers back whenever addressed.
DURR-FULL:v1p571/r3.anchor: {وهو ألد الخصام} أي ذو جدال إذا كلمك راجعك

DURR-FULL:v1p571/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p571/r6.speaker: أبو إسحق
DURR-FULL:v1p571/r6.claim: Abu Ishaq names the Quraysh men who joined in killing Khubayb: ʿIkrima ibn Abi Jahl, Saʿid ibn ʿAbd Allah, al-Akhnas ibn Shariq, ʿUbayda ibn Hakim, and Umayya ibn Abi ʿUtba.
DURR-FULL:v1p571/r6.anchor: عن أبي إسحق قال: كان الذين أجلبوا على خبيب في قتله نفر من قريش

DURR-FULL:v1p572/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p572/r1.speaker: author
DURR-FULL:v1p572/r1.claim: The continuing report says the verse concerns al-Akhnas ibn Shariq, who professed sincere Islam to the Prophet in Medina, impressed him, then burned a Muslim’s crops and hamstrung his donkeys after leaving.
DURR-FULL:v1p572/r1.anchor: قال نزلت في الأخنس بن شريق الثقفي حليف لبني زهرة أقبل إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

DURR-FULL:v1p572/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p572/r2.speaker: الكلبي
DURR-FULL:v1p572/r2.claim: Al-Kalbi says the verse refers to al-Akhnas ibn Shariq; a descendant of al-Akhnas asked him not to name anyone until leaving Mecca, claiming the Qur’an was revealed about Meccans.
DURR-FULL:v1p572/r2.anchor: عن الكلبي قال: كنت جالسا بمكة فسألوني عن هذه الآية

DURR-FULL:v1p572/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p572/r3.speaker: محمد بن كعب القرظي
DURR-FULL:v1p572/r3.claim: Saʿid al-Maqburi quotes a divine warning about honeyed tongues, bitter hearts, and using religion for worldly gain; Muhammad ibn Kaʿb identifies its subject with this verse, and Saʿid says he knew its particular referent.
DURR-FULL:v1p572/r3.anchor: عن أبي سعيد المقبري أنه ذاكر محمد بن كعب القرظي

DURR-FULL:v1p572/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p572/r4.speaker: محمد بن كعب القرظي
DURR-FULL:v1p572/r4.claim: Muhammad ibn Kaʿb says the verse may have been revealed about one man while remaining general in application afterward.
DURR-FULL:v1p572/r4.anchor: فقال محمد بن كعب: إن الآية تنزل في الرجل تكون عامة بعد

DURR-FULL:v1p572/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p572/r5.speaker: الربيع بن أنس
DURR-FULL:v1p572/r5.claim: Al-Rabiʿ ibn Anas transmits a divine warning to a prophet about people with soft sheep skins, honeyed speech, bitter hearts, and false reliance on God; God threatens a bewildering trial and calls believers to trust Him.
DURR-FULL:v1p572/r5.anchor: عن الربيع بن أنس قال: أوحى الله إلى نبي من الأنبياء

DURR-FULL:v1p572/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p572/r6.speaker: وهب
DURR-FULL:v1p572/r6.claim: Wahb reports God rebuking Israelite scholars who pursue worldly gain through religious learning, burden others with religion, and exploit orphans and widows; God swears to send a trial that confounds the wise.
DURR-FULL:v1p572/r6.anchor:
عن وهب
إن الرب تبارك وتعالى قال لعلماء بني إسرائيل

DURR-FULL:v1p573/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p573/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v1p573/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas glosses aladd al-khiṣām as severe in disputation.
DURR-FULL:v1p573/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله {وهو ألد الخصام} قال: شديد الخصومة

DURR-FULL:v1p573/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p573/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v1p573/r2.claim: In response to Nafiʿ ibn al-Azraq, Ibn ʿAbbas explains the phrase as a disputant who argues falsely and cites a line by Muhalhil as Arabic evidence.
DURR-FULL:v1p573/r2.anchor:
عن ابن عباس
أن نافع بن الأزرق سأله قوله {وهو ألد الخصام} قال: الجدل المخاصم في الباطل

DURR-FULL:v1p573/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p573/r3.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v1p573/r3.claim: Mujahid describes the contentious person as unjust and not upright.
DURR-FULL:v1p573/r3.anchor: عن مجاهد {وهو ألد الخصام} قال: ظالم لا يستقيم

DURR-FULL:v1p573/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p573/r4.speaker: عائشة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v1p573/r4.claim: ʿAʾisha reports the Prophet saying that the most hateful men to God are the contentious adversaries.
DURR-FULL:v1p573/r4.anchor: عن عائشة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال أبغض الرجال إلى الله الألد الخصم

DURR-FULL:v1p573/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p573/r5.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v1p573/r5.claim: The Prophet lists four traits of a complete hypocrite: betraying trust, lying, breaking a pact, and speaking abusively in an argument; any one is a trait of hypocrisy until abandoned.
DURR-FULL:v1p573/r5.anchor: عن عبد الله بن عمرو أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: أربع من كن فيه كان منافقا خالصا

DURR-FULL:v1p573/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p573/r6.speaker: ابن عباس عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v1p573/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas reports the Prophet saying that continual disputation is sufficient to make a person sinful.
DURR-FULL:v1p573/r6.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كفى بك آثما

DURR-FULL:v1p573/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p573/r7.speaker: أبو الدرداء
DURR-FULL:v1p573/r7.claim: Abu al-Dardaʾ says continual disputation suffices for sin, continual hostility for injustice, and continual talk about God for lying.
DURR-FULL:v1p573/r7.anchor: عن أبي الدرداء قال: كفى بك آثما أن لا تزال مماريا

DURR-FULL:v1p573/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p573/r8.speaker: أبو الدرداء
DURR-FULL:v1p573/r8.claim: Abu al-Dardaʾ says much speech brings much lying, frequent oaths bring much sin, and frequent quarrels endanger one’s religion.
DURR-FULL:v1p573/r8.anchor: عن أبي الدرداء قال: من كثر كلامه كثر كذبه

DURR-FULL:v1p573/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p573/r9.speaker: عبد الكريم الجزري
DURR-FULL:v1p573/r9.claim: ʿAbd al-Karim al-Jazari says that no scrupulously pious person has ever quarreled.
DURR-FULL:v1p573/r9.anchor: عن عبد الكريم الجزري قال: ما خاصم ورع قط

DURR-FULL:v1p573/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p573/r10.speaker: ابن شبرمة
DURR-FULL:v1p573/r10.claim: Ibn Shubrumah says excessive quarrelling is sinful; he also transmits maxims linking poor restraint in dispute with inability to bear truth and praising patience and chastity.
DURR-FULL:v1p573/r10.anchor: عن ابن شبرمة قال: من بالغ في الخصومة أثم ومن قصر فيها خصم ولا يطيق الحق

DURR-FULL:v1p574/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p574/r1.speaker: الأحنف بن قيس
DURR-FULL:v1p574/r1.claim: Al-Ahnaf ibn Qays says three types cannot prevail fairly over three others, including a forbearing person over a fool and a virtuous person over a profligate.
DURR-FULL:v1p574/r1.anchor: عن الأحنف بن قيس قال: ثلاثة لا ينتصفون من ثلاثة حليم من أحمق وبر من فاجر

DURR-FULL:v1p574/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p574/r2.speaker: ابن عمرو بن العلاء
DURR-FULL:v1p574/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAla says when two men trade insults, the more ignoble one always wins.
DURR-FULL:v1p574/r2.anchor: عن ابن عمرو بن العلاء قال: ما تشاتم رجلان قط إلا غلب ألأمهما

IBNABIHATIM:v2p363/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p363/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v2p363/r1.claim: After the Rajiʿ expedition, a hypocrite mocked the dead; God revealed this passage about their words and the good those men received.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p363/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال : لما اصبيت السريه التي كان فيها عاصم ومرثد بالرجيع

IBNABIHATIM:v2p363/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p363/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v2p363/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the speech is what the person displays of Islam with his tongue.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p363/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال : لما اصبيت السريه التي كان فيها عاصم ومرثد بالرجيع

IBNABIHATIM:v2p363/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p363/r3.speaker: مجاهد وعطاء
IBNABIHATIM:v2p363/r3.claim: Mujāhid and ʿAṭāʾ gloss this as a person's outward presentation in worldly life.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p363/r3.anchor: قال أبو محمد : وروى عن مجاهد وعطاء ، انهما قالا : علانيته في الدنيا

IBNABIHATIM:v2p363/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p363/r4.speaker: أبو العالية
IBNABIHATIM:v2p363/r4.claim: Abū al-ʿĀliya describes a man with good speech but bad deeds who speaks well to the Prophet.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p363/r4.anchor: عن ابي العالية : ومن الناس من يعجبك قوله في الحياة الدنيا قال : كان هذا عبد حسن القول ، سيء الفعل

IBNABIHATIM:v2p363/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p363/r5.speaker: رسول الله
IBNABIHATIM:v2p363/r5.claim: The Prophet warns of honeyed tongues, bitter hearts, worldly exploitation of religion, and a trial that confounds the forbearing.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p363/r5.anchor: عن محمد بن كعب القرظي ، قال : قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : ان لله عبادا السنتهم احلا من العسل

IBNABIHATIM:v2p363/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p363/r6.speaker: السدي
IBNABIHATIM:v2p363/r6.claim: Al-Suddī says the verse was revealed about Akhnas ibn Shurayq, an ally of Banū Zuhra.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p363/r6.anchor: عن السدى : ومن الناس من يعجبك قوله في الحياة الدنيا قال : نزلت في اخنس بن شريق الثقفي

IBNABIHATIM:v2p363/r7.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p363/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v2p363/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the heart contradicts what the person says with his tongue.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p363/r7.anchor: عن ابن عباس ، قوله : ويشهد الله على ما في قلبه انه لمخالف لما يقول بلسانه

IBNABIHATIM:v2p364/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p364/r1.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v2p364/r1.claim: Mujāhid says he invokes God as witness in a dispute while claiming to want only truth.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p364/r1.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح عن مجاهد ، ويشهد الله في الخصومة ، انما يريد للحق

IBNABIHATIM:v2p364/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p364/r2.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v2p364/r2.claim: Qatāda identifies the person as a hypocrite.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p364/r2.anchor: عن قتادة ويشهد الله على ما في قلبه قال : هو المنافق

IBNABIHATIM:v2p364/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p364/r3.speaker: السدي
IBNABIHATIM:v2p364/r3.claim: Al-Suddī says Akhnas claimed to the Prophet that he sought Islam and was truthful.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p364/r3.anchor: عن السدى ، قوله : ويشهد الله علي ما في قلبه قال : اقبل الاخنس بن شريق الى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNABIHATIM:v2p364/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p364/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v2p364/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses the phrase as a skilled debater who answers back.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p364/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس وهو الد الخصام اي : ذو جدال اذا كلمك وراجعك

IBNABIHATIM:v2p364/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p364/r5.speaker: الضحاك عن ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v2p364/r5.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk reports Ibn ʿAbbās's gloss: severe in disputation.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p364/r5.anchor: عن أبي روق ، عن الضحاك ، عن ابن عباس ، يقول : شديد الخصومة

IBNABIHATIM:v2p364/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p364/r6.speaker: الحسن
IBNABIHATIM:v2p364/r6.claim: Al-Ḥasan interprets the phrase as lying speech.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p364/r6.anchor: عن عاصم ، عن الحسن : وهو الد الخصام قال : كاذب القول

IBNABIHATIM:v2p364/r7.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p364/r7.speaker: محمد بن كعب
IBNABIHATIM:v2p364/r7.claim: Muḥammad ibn Kaʿb is reported to give al-Ḥasan's gloss of lying speech.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p364/r7.anchor: وروى عن محمد بن كعب ، نحو قول الحسن

IBNABIHATIM:v2p364/r8.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p364/r8.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v2p364/r8.claim: Mujāhid says the person is unjust and not upright.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p364/r8.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح عن مجاهد قوله / الد الخصام ظالم لا يستقيم

IBNABIHATIM:v2p364/r9.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p364/r9.speaker: عطاء الخراساني
IBNABIHATIM:v2p364/r9.claim: ʿAṭāʾ al-Khurāsānī is reported to give Mujāhid's gloss.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p364/r9.anchor: وروى عن عطاء الخراساني ، نحو قول مجاهد

IBNABIHATIM:v2p364/r10.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p364/r10.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v2p364/r10.claim: Qatāda describes him as hard-hearted in disobedience and argumentative in falsehood.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p364/r10.anchor: عن قتادة 1 : وهو الد الخصام قال : شديد القسوة في معصيته لله ، جدل بالباطل

IBNABIHATIM:v2p364/r11.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p364/r11.speaker: السدي
IBNABIHATIM:v2p364/r11.claim: Al-Suddī glosses the phrase as crooked disputation.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p364/r11.anchor: عن السدى : وهو الد الخصام فاعوج الخصام

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p204/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p204/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p204/r1.claim: The discourse groups Jews, Christians, and polytheists in resentment of Muslims, then distinguishes Jewish-Christian disputes; polytheists are worst for obstructing worship at the sanctuary and sharing hostility to Islam.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p204/r1.anchor: ثم قرن اليهود والنصارى والمشركون في قرن حسدهم المسلمين والسخط على الشريعة الجديدة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p204/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p204/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p204/r2.claim: The discussion turns to the sanctuary, Abraham and his prayer for descendants, Islam as Abrahamic monotheism, the Kaaba's qibla and Meccan rites; Judaism and Christianity are not Abraham's religion.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p204/r2.anchor: وانتقل بهذه المناسبة إلى فضائل المسجد الحرام

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p204/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p204/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p204/r3.claim: The change of qibla rebuts the People of the Book; purifying souls matters more than facing east or west, and replacing earlier laws with what benefits later peoples is no novelty.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p204/r3.anchor: وأن العناية بتزكية النفوس أجدر من العناية باستقبال الجهات

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p204/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p204/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p204/r4.claim: The argument returns to creation, the disavowal of leaders on Judgment Day, and food prohibitions, ending with people who do not profess Islam but display affection toward Muslims.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p204/r4.anchor: ثم عاد إلى محاجة المشركين بالاستدلال بآثار صنعة الله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p263/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p263/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p263/r6.claim: Al-Akhnas ibn Shariq al-Thaqafi outwardly displayed affection and faith; Ibn Ashur says his case will be discussed under 2:204.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p263/r6.anchor: والأخنس أبي بن شريق الثقفي كان يظهر الود والإيمان وسيأتي عند قوله تعالى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p264/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p264/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p264/r2.claim: Because the passage begins with Hajj regulations and ends with the days of pilgrimage and return home, the charge to fear God is for returning pilgrims to keep piety in every place and situation, not only during Hajj; pre-Islamic Arabs and some Muslims lapse after sacred seasons.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p264/r2.anchor: وصية جامعة للراجعين من الحج أن يراقبوا تقوى الله في سائر أحوالهم وأماكنهم ولا يجعلوا تقواه خاصة بمدة الحج

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p273/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p273/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p273/r6.claim: The passage teaches believers to discern inner realities and not be deceived by appearances before testing: a person may speak sweetly and look good while concealing evil and plotting harm.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p10#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p10#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p10#2/r1.claim: When a geminated verb is intransitive, its form usually signals abundance or intensification; the Shafiya states this rule, though abundance can be figurative.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p10#2/r1.anchor: بناء على أن فعل المضاعف إذا لم يكن للتعدية كان المقصود منه الدلالة على التكثير من المصدر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p10#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p10#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p10#2/r2.claim: Figurative intensification can treat intellectual labor—finding subtle meanings and choosing exact expression—as extensive work.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p10#2/r2.anchor: وقد يكون التكثير في ذلك مجازيا واعتباريا بأن ينزل كد الفكر في تحصيل المعاني الدقيقة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p10#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p10#2/r3.speaker: صحار العبدي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p10#2/r3.claim: Asked by Muawiya about eloquence, Ṣaḥār al-ʿAbdī said to speak without error and answer without delay, then jokingly asked to retract the demand to do both.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p10#2/r3.anchor: كتفسير صحار العبدي وقد سأله معاوية عن البلاغة فقال : أن تقول فلا تخطئ ، وتجيب فلا تبطئ

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p10#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p10#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p10#2/r4.claim: The intensive sense of verbal explanation is supported by the Quran’s phrase أحسن تفسيرا in 25:33.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p10#2/r4.anchor: ويشهد لهذا قوله تعالى ) ولا يأتونك بمثل إلا جئناك بالحق وأحسن تفسيرا (

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p10#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p10#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p10#2/r5.claim: Whether gemination intensifies a transitive verb is disputed; Ibn Ashur says a speaker may choose it over hamza to imply abundance by association with its intransitive use.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p10#2/r5.anchor: فأما إذا كان فعل المضاعف للتعدية فإن إفادته التكثير مختلف فيها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p10#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p10#2/r8.speaker: بعض مشايخ القرافي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p10#2/r8.claim: A teacher cited by al-Qarafi distinguishes light فرق for meanings and doubled فرّق for bodies, reasoning that more letters convey greater or stronger meaning.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p10#2/r8.anchor: وعزا شهاب الدين القرافي في أول أنواء البروق إلى بعض مشايخه أن العرب فرقوا بين فرق

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p10#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p10#2/r9.speaker: القرافي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p10#2/r9.claim: Al-Qarafi objects that the light-versus-heavy distinction does not hold consistently.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p10#2/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p10#2/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p10#2/r10.claim: Ibn Ashur rejects that distinction as rhetorical nicety rather than sound rule: the forms signal real or figurative abundance, not abstract meanings versus physical objects.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p10#2/r10.anchor: بل هو أشبه باللطائف منه بالحقائق

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p10#2/r12.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p10#2/r12.speaker: لبيد
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p10#2/r12.claim: Labid’s line pairs the verb قدم with its noun إقدام, illustrating alternation between related verb forms.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p10#2/r12.anchor: وقال لبيد : فمضى وقدمها وكانت عادة منه إذا هي عردت إقدامها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p10#2/r13.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p10#2/r13.speaker: سيبويه
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p10#2/r13.claim: Sibawayh says فعل and أفعل alternate; the proposed distinction concerns the verb’s meaning, not whether its object is a body.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p10#2/r13.anchor: وقال سيبويه إن فعل وأفعل يتعاقبان على أن التفرقة عند مثبتها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p10#2/r14.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p10#2/r14.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p10#2/r14.claim: In technical usage, tafsir is the discipline that explains Quranic words and meanings derived from them, briefly or at length.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p10#2/r14.anchor: والتفسير في الاصطلاح نقول : هو اسم للعلم الباحث عن بيان معاني ألفاظ القرآن

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p10#2/r15.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p10#2/r15.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p10#2/r15.claim: The relation between lexical and technical senses of tafsir needs little explanation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p10#2/r15.anchor: والمناسبة بين المعنى الأصلي والمعنى المنقول إليه لا يحتاج إلى تطويل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p10#2/r16.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p10#2/r16.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p10#2/r16.claim: Tafsir’s subject is Quranic wording as examined for meaning and inference.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p10#2/r17.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p10#2/r17.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p10#2/r17.claim: Tafsir differs from qira’at because disciplines are distinguished by their subjects and the aspects from which they examine them.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p10#2/r18.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p10#2/r18.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p10#2/r18.claim: Calling tafsir a science is loose: knowledge may mean cognition, the rational faculty, certain belief, or demonstrable universal propositions, none of which describes tafsir’s material.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p10#2/r18.anchor: هذا وفي عد التفسير علما تسامح

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p10#2/r19.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p10#2/r19.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p10#2/r19.claim: Tafsir usually treats particular concepts, not provable universal propositions: explaining words is verbal definition, while derivation proceeds by entailment.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p10#2/r19.anchor: فأما تفسير الألفاظ فهو من قبيل التعريف اللفظي

IBNMAJAH:3930/r1.author: IBNMAJAH
IBNMAJAH:3930/r1.speaker: النبي
IBNMAJAH:3930/r1.claim: Imran b. Husayn recounts the Prophet rebuking a fighter who killed a man after he professed Islam: no one can inspect his heart; the man's body repeatedly rose from its grave.
IBNMAJAH:3930/r1.anchor: فَقَالَ لَهُ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ـ صلى الله عليه وسلم ـ ‏"‏ فَهَلاَّ شَقَقْتَ عَنْ بَطْنِهِ فَعَلِمْتَ مَا فِي قَلْبِهِ ‏"‏

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p278#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p278#2/r1.speaker: السدي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p278#2/r1.claim: Al-Suddi says the passage concerns al-Akhnas ibn Shurayq (whose name he gives as Ubay): he professed Islam, claimed sincerity, then burned Muslim crops and killed their donkeys.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p278#2/r1.anchor: قال السدي: «نزلت في الأخنس بن شريق، واسمه أبي، والأخنس لقب،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p278#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p278#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p278#2/r2.claim: The author says it is not established that al-Akhnas ever became Muslim.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p278#2/r2.anchor: قال القاضي أبو محمد عبد الحق رضي الله عنه: ما ثبت قط أن الأخنس أسلم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p278#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p278#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p278#2/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says the first passage describes hypocrites who disparaged those killed at al-Rajiʿ, naming ʿAsim ibn Thabit, Khubayb, and Ibn al-Dathinna; the following verse refers to its martyrs.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p278#2/r3.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: نزلت في قوم من المنافقين تكلموا في الذين قتلوا في غزوة الرجيع عاصم بن ثابت

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p278#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p278#2/r4.speaker: قتادة ومجاهد وجماعة من العلماء
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p278#2/r4.claim: Qatada, Mujahid, and other scholars generalize the passage to anyone concealing unbelief, hypocrisy, lies, or harm while speaking otherwise.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p278#2/r4.anchor: وقال قتادة ومجاهد وجماعة من العلماء: نزلت هذه الآيات في كل مبطن كفر أو نفاق

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p278#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p278#2/r5.speaker: الترمذي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p278#2/r5.claim: A report cited in al-Tirmidhi from a divine book describes people with honey-sweet tongues and bitter hearts, who use religion for worldly gain and face a confounding trial.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p278#2/r5.anchor: وهي تشبه ما ورد في الترمذي أن في بعض كتب الله تعالى: «أن من عباد الله قوما ألسنتهم أحلى من العسل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p278#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p278#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p278#2/r6.claim: “He calls God to witness” means the person claims, “God knows I am telling the truth.”
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p278#2/r6.anchor: ومعنى ويشهد الله أي يقول: الله يعلم أني أقول حقا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p278#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p278#2/r7.speaker: أبو حيوة وابن محيصن
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p278#2/r7.claim: Abu Haywa and Ibn Muhaysin attribute the verb to God: God knows the speaker’s words contradict his reality; this reading makes the concealed evil the heart’s content.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p278#2/r7.anchor: وقرأ أبو حيوة وابن محيصن «ويشهد الله» بإسناد الفعل إلى اسم الجلالة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p278#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p278#2/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p278#2/r8.claim: The majority reading more sharply condemns one who deliberately adopts good speech while inwardly contradicting it; he claims goodness in his heart.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p278#2/r8.anchor: والقراءة التي للجماعة أبلغ في ذمه، لأنه قوى على نفسه التزام الكلام الحسن

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p278#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p278#2/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p278#2/r9.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas reads “God witnesses what is in his heart.”
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p278#2/r9.anchor: وقرأ ابن عباس «والله يشهد على ما في قلبه»

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p278#2/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p278#2/r10.speaker: أبي وابن مسعود
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p278#2/r10.claim: Ubayy and Ibn Masʿud read that the speaker calls God as witness to what is in his heart.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p278#2/r10.anchor: وقرأ أبي وابن مسعود «ويستشهد الله على ما في قلبه»

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p278#2/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p278#2/r11.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p278#2/r11.claim: Al-add is a fierce, stubborn disputant who twists arguments in every direction; related expressions evoke the sides of a valley, the mouth, and a draught.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p278#2/r11.anchor: والألد: الشديد الخصومة الصعب الشكيمة الذي يلوي الحجج في كل جانب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p278#2/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p278#2/r12.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p278#2/r12.claim: The Prophet said the most hateful men to God are the stubborn disputant.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p278#2/r12.anchor: ومنه قول النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: «أبغض الرجال إلى الله الألد الخصم»

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p279/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p279/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p279/r1.claim: Al-khiṣām can be the verbal noun of khāṣama or a plural of khaṣm, making the phrase mean the most forceful of adversaries.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p279/r1.anchor: والخصام في الآية مصدر خاصم، وقيل جمع خصم ككلب وكلاب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p279/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p279/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p279/r2.claim: An unnamed poet’s line uses “a stubborn adversary” to illustrate al-add as a description of a fierce opponent.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p281/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p281/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p281/r8.claim: The preceding verses appear to concern unbelievers generally; sinners sharing these traits also incur a portion of the warning.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p281/r8.anchor: والظاهر من هذا التقسيم أن تكون الآيات قبل هذا على العموم في الكافر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p281/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p281/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p281/r9.claim: If the earlier verses concern hypocrites who spoke about al-Rajiʿ, this one concerns its martyrs; if they concern al-Akhnas, this one concerns the first Anṣar and Muhājirūn to believe.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p281/r9.anchor: ومن قال إن الآيات المتقدمة هي في منافقين تكلموا في غزوة الرجيع

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p218#3/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p218#3/r1.speaker: ابن عباس والسدي ومقاتل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p218#3/r1.claim: They say the verse concerns al-Akhnas ibn Shurayq, whose gentle speech and professions of love and following Islam concealed unbelief and hostility.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p218#3/r1.anchor: وهو يضمر غير ذلك هذا قول ابن عباس والسدي و مقاتل

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p218#3/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p218#3/r2.speaker: الحسن وقتادة وابن زيد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p218#3/r2.claim: Al-Hasan, Qatada, and Ibn Zayd take the verse generally as concerning a hypocrite whose outward speech differs from his heart.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p218#3/r2.anchor: والثاني أنها نزلت فيمن نافق فأظهر بلسانه ما ليس في قلبه وهذا قول الحسن وقتادة وابن زيد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p218#3/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p218#3/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p218#3/r3.claim: A third occasion is the Rajiʿ expedition: Quraysh falsely claimed conversion and asked Muhammad to send teachers to instruct them.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p218#3/r3.anchor: والثالث أنها نزلت في سرية الرجيع وذلك أن كفار قريش بعثوا إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وهو بالمدينة إنا قد أسلمنا فابعث لنا نفرا من أصحابك يعلمونا ديننا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p218#3/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p218#3/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p218#3/r4.claim: The Prophet sent Khubayb ibn ʿAdi, Marthad al-Ghanawi, Khalid ibn Bukayr, Abdullah ibn Tariq, and Zayd ibn al-Dathina, with ʿAsim ibn Thabit as their commander.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p218#3/r4.anchor: فبعث صلى الله عليه وسلم خبيب بن عدي ومرثدا الغنوي وخالد بن بكير وعبد الله بن طارق وزيد بن الدثنة وأمر عليهم عاصم بن ثابت

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p218#3/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p218#3/r5.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p218#3/r5.claim: After the group ate dates, a passing woman saw their pits, alerted her people, and seventy men surrounded them between Mecca and Medina.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p218#3/r5.anchor: ومعهم تمر فأكلوا منه فمرت عجوز فأبصرت النوى فرجعت إلى قومها وقالت قد سلك هذا الطريق أهل يثرب فركب سبعون منهم حتى أحاطوا بهم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p218#3/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p218#3/r6.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p218#3/r6.claim: In the fighting, Marthad, Khalid, and Ibn Tariq were killed; ʿAsim shot seven leaders with his seven arrows before the attackers killed him.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p218#3/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p218#3/r7.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p218#3/r7.claim: ʿAsim prayed that God protect his body after defending God's religion; the attackers sought his head for Salafa bint Saʿd, whose family he had killed, but wasps kept them away.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p218#3/r7.anchor: فأرسل الله تعالى رجلا من الدبر وهي الزنابير فحمته

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p218#3/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p218#3/r8.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p218#3/r8.claim: The attackers waited for evening, but a cloud brought heavy rain and a flood carried ʿAsim's body away.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p218#3/r8.anchor: فقال دعوه حتى يمسي فتذهب عنه فنأخذه فجاءت سحابة فأمطرت كالعزالي فبعث الله الوادي فاحتمله فذهب به

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p218#3/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p218#3/r9.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p218#3/r9.claim: Khubayb and Zayd were captured; Banu al-Harith bought Khubayb to kill him because he had killed their fathers.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p218#3/r9.anchor: وأسروا خبيبا وزيدا فابتاع بنو الحارث

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p218#3/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p218#3/r10.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p218#3/r10.claim: Before his execution, Khubayb requested two units of prayer, then declined to lengthen them lest onlookers call him afraid and recited a poem accepting death for God.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p218#3/r10.anchor: فلما خرجوا به ليقتلوه قال دعوني أصلي ركعتين فتركوه فصلى ركعتين ثم قال لولا أن تقولوا جزع خبيب لزدت وأنشأ يقول ولست أبالي حين أقتل مسلما على أي شق كان في الله مصرعي

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p220/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p220/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p220/r1.claim: Khubayb was crucified alive and asked God to deliver his greeting to the Messenger; when Abu Suruʿa put a spear before him and told him to fear God, it only increased his defiance.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p220/r1.anchor: فصلبوه حيا فقال اللهم إنك تعلم أنه ليس أحد حولي يبلغ رسولك سلامي فجاءه رجل منهم يقال له أبو سروعة ومعه رمح فوضعه بين يدي خبيب فقال له خبيب اتق الله فما زاده ذلك إلا عتوا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p220/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p220/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p220/r2.claim: Safwan ibn Umayya bought Zayd to avenge his father; Abu Sufyan asked if Zayd would prefer Muhammad in his place, and Zayd answered that he would not wish Muhammad harmed by even a thorn while Zayd was home.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p220/r2.anchor: وأما زيد فابتاعه صفوان بن أمية ليقتله بأبيه فجاءه سفيان بن حرب حين قدم ليقتله فقال يا زيد أنشدك الله أتحب أن محمدا مكانك وأنك في أهلك فقال والله ما أحب أن محمدا الآن في مكانه الذي هو فيه تصيبه شوكة تؤذيه وأنا جالس في أهلي

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p220/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p220/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p220/r3.claim: After Zayd was killed, the Prophet asked who would recover Khubayb from his gallows for Paradise; al-Zubayr and al-Miqdad went to retrieve him.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p220/r3.anchor: ثم قتل وبلغ النبي الخبر فقال أيكم يحتمل خبيبا عن خشبته وله الجنة فقال الزبير أنا وصاحبي المقداد فخرجا يمشيان بالليل

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p220/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p220/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p220/r4.claim: They found forty pagan men sleeping drunk around the gallows and Khubayb's body still fresh and flexible after forty days.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p220/r4.anchor: لم يتغير فيه شيء بعد أربعين يوما

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p220/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p220/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p220/r5.claim: Al-Zubayr carried Khubayb on his horse; when seventy pursuers caught up, he dropped the body and the earth swallowed it.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p220/r5.anchor: فحمله الزبير على فرسه وسار فلحقه سبعون منهم فقذف الزبير خبيبا فابتلعته الأرض

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p220/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p220/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p220/r6.claim: Al-Zubayr identified himself and al-Miqdad as lions protecting their young and offered combat or safe departure; the pursuers left.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p220/r6.anchor: ثم رفع العمامة عن رأسه وقال أنا الزبير بن العوام وأمي صفية بنت عبد المطلب وصاحبي المقداد أسدان رابضان يدفعان عن شبلهما فان شئتم ناضلتكم وإن شئتم نازلتكم وإن شئتم انصرفتم فانصرفوا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p220/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p220/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p220/r7.claim: When the two reached the Prophet, Gabriel was with him and said the angels were boasting of these two companions.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p220/r7.anchor: جبريل عنده فقال يا محمد إن الملائكة لتباهي بهذين من أصحابك

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p220/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p220/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p220/r8.claim: Some hypocrites mocked the slain men for not staying home and for failing to deliver their companion's message.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p220/r8.anchor: وقال بعض المنافقين في أصحاب خبيب ويح هؤلاء المقتولين لا في بيوتهم قعدوا ولا رسالة صاحبهم أدوا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p220/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p220/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p220/r9.claim: The report says this verse and the next three were revealed concerning al-Zubayr, al-Miqdad, Khubayb and the other expedition members, as well as the hypocrites.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p220/r9.anchor: فأنزل الله تعالى في الزبير والمقداد وخبيب وأصحابه والمنافقين هذه الآية وثلاث آيات بعدها وهذا الحديث بطوله مروي عن ابن عباس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p221/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p221/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p221/r1.claim: One interpretation is that he says God witnesses that his tongue expresses what is in his heart.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p221/r1.anchor: فيه قولان أحدهما أنه يقول إن الله يشهد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p221/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p221/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p221/r2.claim: Another interpretation is that he asks God to witness his statement.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p221/r2.anchor: والثاني أنه يقول اللهم اشهد علي بهذا القول

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p221/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p221/r3.speaker: ابن مسعود
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p221/r3.claim: Ibn Masʿud's reading adds sin and ta, yielding yastashhidu Allah (“he calls God to witness”).
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p221/r3.anchor: وقرأ ابن مسعود ويستشهد الله بزيادة سين وتاء

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p221/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p221/r4.speaker: الحسن وطلحة بن مصرف وابن محيصن وابن عبلة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p221/r4.claim: Al-Hasan and the other named readers read yashhadu with an open ya and Allah in the nominative.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p221/r4.anchor: وقرأ الحسن وطلحة بن مصرف وابن محيصن وابن عبلة ويشهد بفتح الياء الله بالرفع

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p221/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p221/r5.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p221/r5.claim: Al-Zajjaj notes that khisam is a plural form of khasm, with khusum also used.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p221/r5.anchor: الخصام جمع خصم يقال خصم وخصام وخصوم قال الزجاج

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p221/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p221/r6.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p221/r6.claim: Al-Zajjaj says al-add means intensely contentious; the image derives from the two sides of the neck, since this opponent wins whichever path of argument is taken.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p562#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p562#2/r1.speaker: السدي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p562#2/r1.claim: Al-Suddi says the verse was revealed about al-Akhnas ibn Shurayq, who professed Islam to the Prophet while concealing the opposite.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p562#2/r1.anchor: قال السدي: نزلت في الأخنس بن شريق الثقفي، جاء إلى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p562#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p562#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p562#2/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says it concerned hypocrites who disparaged Khubayb and his companions, killed at al-Raji; the verses condemn them and praise Khubayb's companions.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p562#2/r2.anchor: وعن ابن عباس: أنها نزلت في نفر من المنافقين تكلموا في خبيب وأصحابه الذين قتلوا بالرجيع

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p562#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p562#2/r3.speaker: قتادة، ومجاهد، والربيع ابن أنس وغير واحد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p562#2/r3.claim: They take the contrast as general: the hypocrites' traits apply to hypocrites broadly and the self-sacrifice to believers broadly; Ibn Kathir calls this correct.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p562#2/r3.anchor: بل ذلك عام في المنافقين كلهم وفي المؤمنين كلهم. وهذا قول قتادة، ومجاهد، والربيع ابن أنس، وغير واحد، وهو الصحيح

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p562#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p562#2/r4.speaker: نوف البكالي
