IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p562#2/r4.claim: Nauf says scripture describes people who pursue worldly gain through religion, with honeyed tongues and bitter hearts, sheep-like exteriors and wolf-like hearts; God warns of a trial that confounds the wise.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p562#2/r4.anchor: عن نوف -وهو البكالي، وكان ممن يقرأ الكتب -قال: إني لأجد صفة ناس من هذه الأمة في كتاب الله المنزل

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p562#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p562#2/r5.speaker: القرظي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p562#2/r5.claim: Al-Qurazi identifies those described in the earlier scripture report as the hypocrites and finds their description in this verse.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p562#2/r5.anchor: قال القرظي: تدبرتها في القرآن، فإذا هم المنافقون، فوجدتها: {ومن الناس من يعجبك قوله

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p562#2/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p562#2/r6.speaker: سعيد المقبري ومحمد بن كعب القرظي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p562#2/r6.claim: Sa'id al-Maqburi recounts a saying from earlier books about religious opportunists; Muhammad ibn Ka'b says the description is in the Quran, at this verse.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p562#2/r6.anchor: سمعت سعيدا المقبري يذاكر محمد بن كعب القرظي، فقال سعيد: إن في بعض الكتب

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p562#2/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p562#2/r7.speaker: محمد بن كعب
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p562#2/r7.claim: Muhammad ibn Ka'b says a verse may be revealed about one man and thereafter have general application.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p562#2/r7.anchor: قال محمد بن كعب: إن الآية تنزل في الرجل، ثم تكون عامة بعد

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p562#2/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p562#2/r8.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p562#2/r8.claim: Ibn Kathir judges al-Qurazi's explanation sound and correct.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p562#2/r8.anchor: وهذا الذي قاله القرظي حسن صحيح

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p563/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p563/r1.speaker: ابن محيصن
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p563/r1.claim: Ibn Muhaysin reads the verb with an open yāʾ and Allah in the nominative, making God the one who witnesses what is in the heart.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p563/r1.anchor: فقرأه ابن محيصن: "ويشهد الله" بفتح الياء، وضم الجلالة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p563/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p563/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p563/r2.claim: On Ibn Muhaysin's reading, the hypocrite's guile may deceive people, but God knows the evil in his heart, as in the description of hypocrites in 63:1.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p563/r2.anchor: هذا وإن أظهر لكم الحيل (2) لكن الله يعلم من قلبه القبيح

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p563/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p563/r3.speaker: الجمهور
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p563/r3.claim: The majority reading has a passive-form verb and Allah in the accusative: the person calls God to witness concerning his heart.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p563/r3.anchor: وقراءة الجمهور بضم الياء، ونصب الجلالة {ويشهد الله على ما في قلبه}

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p563/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p563/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p563/r4.claim: On the majority reading, he presents Islam publicly while openly confronting God with inward unbelief and hypocrisy; Ibn Kathir links this to 4:108.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p563/r4.anchor: يظهر للناس الإسلام ويبارز الله بما في قلبه من الكفر والنفاق

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p563/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p563/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p563/r5.claim: Ibn Kathir says the explanation that the hypocrite openly confronts God with his inward state is transmitted from Ibn Abbas through the report of Ibn Ishaq.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p563/r5.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير، عن ابن عباس

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p563/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p563/r6.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن زيد بن أسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p563/r6.claim: He means the person swears before people, calling God to witness that his heart agrees with his tongue; Ibn Kathir calls this sound, and Ibn Jarir prefers it, also attributing it to Ibn Abbas and Mujahid.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p563/r6.anchor: وقالَه عبد الرحمن بن زيد بن أسلم، واختاره ابن جرير

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p563#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p563#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p563#2/r1.claim: Al-ald means crooked; like the ludd in 19:97, a hypocrite in dispute lies, turns from truth, fabricates, and transgresses.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p563#2/r1.anchor: الألد في اللغة: [هو] (4) الأعوج، {وتنذر به قوما لدا}

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p563#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p563#2/r2.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p563#2/r2.claim: A sound Prophetic report gives lying when speaking, betrayal when pledged, and wickedness in dispute as three signs of a hypocrite.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p563#2/r2.anchor: كما ثبت في الصحيح عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال: "آية المنافق ثلاث

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p563#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p563#2/r3.speaker: عائشة عن النبي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p563#2/r3.claim: Aisha reports from the Prophet that the most hateful man to God is the fiercely disputatious opponent; al-Bukhari transmits it through multiple routes, as does Abd al-Razzaq.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p563#2/r3.anchor: عن ابن أبي مليكة، عن عائشة ترفعه قال: "أبغض الرجال إلى الله الألد الخصم"

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p564/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p564/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p564/r1.claim: The hypocrite's crooked speech is matched by evil action: his words are lies, belief corrupt, and deeds ugly.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p564/r1.anchor: هو أعوج المقال، سيئ الفعال، فذلك قوله، وهذا فعله: كلامه كذب، واعتقاده فاسد، وأفعاله قبيحة

JISHUMI:v1p833#2/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p833#2/r1.speaker: أبي
JISHUMI:v1p833#2/r1.claim: The standard reading has yāʾ with ḍamma and Allah nominative; Ubayy's codex reads yastashhidu Allah, an explanatory rendering of the common reading.
JISHUMI:v1p833#2/r1.anchor: القراءة الظاهرة المجمع عليها (ويشهد) بضم الياء من أشهد ويشهد بفتح الياء. والهاء، الله رفع، وفي مصحف أبي ويستشهد الله

JISHUMI:v1p833#2/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p833#2/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p833#2/r3.claim: Aʿjabahu means to please or impress; wonder concerns what is outside the ordinary.
JISHUMI:v1p833#2/r3.anchor: أعجبه كذا إعجابا، والعجب ما يتعجب منه، ويكون خلاف العادة

JISHUMI:v1p833#2/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p833#2/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p833#2/r4.claim: Al-add means extreme contentiousness, from ladata in the sense of intense dispute; the phrase قوما لدا is cited.
JISHUMI:v1p833#2/r4.anchor: والألد: الشديد الخصومة، لددت لدا، وهو أشد الخصومة، ومنه: (قوما لدا)

JISHUMI:v1p833#2/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p833#2/r5.speaker: الزجاج
JISHUMI:v1p833#2/r5.claim: Al-Zajjaj takes khiṣām as the plural of khaṣm, yielding 'the fiercest of disputants.'
JISHUMI:v1p833#2/r5.anchor: والخصام: جمع خصم، عند الزجاج، وهو من الخصومة، وكأنه قيل: هو أشد المخاصمين خصومة

JISHUMI:v1p833#2/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p833#2/r6.speaker: الخليل
JISHUMI:v1p833#2/r6.claim: Al-Khalil instead treats khiṣām as a verbal noun from khāṣamahu, he disputed with him.
JISHUMI:v1p833#2/r6.anchor: وقيل: هو مصدر، عن الخليل، ويقول: خاصمه خصاما

JISHUMI:v1p833#2/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p833#2/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p833#2/r8.claim: Ashhada yushhidu means to acknowledge something before another person so they can witness it.
JISHUMI:v1p833#2/r8.anchor: وأشهد يشهدة إشهادا إذا أقر عند غيره ليشهد به

JISHUMI:v1p833#2/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p833#2/r10.speaker: السدي والكلبي
JISHUMI:v1p833#2/r10.claim: Al-Suddi and al-Kalbi say the verse concerns al-Akhnas al-Thaqafi, an ally of Banu Zuhra, whose name was Ubayy; he persuaded them to withdraw from Badr by saying Muhammad was their nephew, then charmed the Prophet with public Islam while concealing hostility.
JISHUMI:v1p833#2/r10.anchor: نزلت في الأخنس الثقفي حليف بني زهرة، واسمه أمي، عن السدي والكلبي

JISHUMI:v1p833#2/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p833#2/r12.speaker: ابن عباس والضحاك
JISHUMI:v1p833#2/r12.claim: Ibn Abbas and al-Dahhak connect the verse to the al-Rajiʿ expedition: Quraysh falsely claimed conversion and requested learned Companions, so the Prophet sent a party including Khubayb ibn ʿAdi.
JISHUMI:v1p833#2/r12.anchor: وعن ابن عباس والضحاك: نزلت في سرية الرجيع، وذلك أن كفار قريش بعثوا إلى النبي

JISHUMI:v1p835/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p835/r1.speaker: الحسن
JISHUMI:v1p835/r1.claim: Al-Hasan says the verse concerns hypocrites.
JISHUMI:v1p835/r1.anchor: وقيل: نزلت الآية في المنافقين، عن الحسن

JISHUMI:v1p835/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p835/r2.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v1p835/r2.claim: Another view says it concerns people who deceive by their tongues and then commit injustice and corruption when they leave.
JISHUMI:v1p835/r2.anchor: وقيل: في المرائين يخدعون بلسانهم، فإذا تولوا ظلموا وأفسدوا

JISHUMI:v1p835/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p835/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p835/r3.claim: After describing believers and unbelievers, the passage turns to hypocrites.
JISHUMI:v1p835/r3.anchor: ثم بين تعالى حال المنافقين بعد ذكر أحوال المؤمنين والكافرين

JISHUMI:v1p835/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p835/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p835/r4.claim: The speech pleases Muhammad and looms large in his heart; the speaker claims belief and loyalty, and invokes God as witness while inwardly concealing the opposite.
JISHUMI:v1p835/r4.anchor: أي تستحسن كلامه يا محمد، ويعظم في قلبك، والعجب كل شيء يعظم في قلبك

JISHUMI:v1p835/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p835/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p835/r5.claim: The phrase means he says 'God is my witness' while his inward state contradicts his outward speech.
JISHUMI:v1p835/r5.anchor: يعني يضمر خلاف ما يظهر من القول فبإضماره يشهد الله على ذلك

JISHUMI:v1p835/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p835/r6.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v1p835/r6.claim: One interpretation is that he is severe in disputation.

JISHUMI:v1p835/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p835/r7.speaker: مجاهد
JISHUMI:v1p835/r7.claim: Mujahid says he is crooked in argument and does not remain consistent in a dispute.
JISHUMI:v1p835/r7.anchor: أعوج في الخصومة لا يستقيم على خصومة عن مجاهد

JISHUMI:v1p835/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p835/r8.speaker: الحسن
JISHUMI:v1p835/r8.claim: Al-Hasan interprets the phrase as 'a liar.'

JISHUMI:v1p835/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p835/r9.speaker: قتادة
JISHUMI:v1p835/r9.claim: Qatada says he is hard-hearted in disobeying God and argues falsely.
JISHUMI:v1p835/r9.anchor: شديد القسوة في معصية الله جدل بالباطل، عن قتادة

JISHUMI:v1p835/r19.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p835/r19.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p835/r19.claim: The passage shows hypocrisy is religiously blameworthy and faith is not mere profession.
JISHUMI:v1p835/r19.anchor: الآية تدل على أن النفاق يقبح في الدين. تدل على أن الإيمان ليس بمجرد قول

JISHUMI:v1p835/r20.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p835/r20.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p835/r20.claim: A person may be judged Muslim outwardly even while privately concealing the opposite.
JISHUMI:v1p835/r20.anchor: وتدل على جواز أن يحكم له بالإسلام في الظاهر، وإن كان يستسر خلافه

JISHUMI:v1p835/r21.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p835/r21.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p835/r21.claim: The Prophet does not know the unseen, and an Imam is even less entitled to that claim; this refutes the Imamiyya.
JISHUMI:v1p835/r21.anchor: وتدل على أن النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - لا يعلم الغيب، فيكون الإمام أولى بذلك، فيبطل قول الإمامية

JISHUMI:v1p835/r22.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p835/r22.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p835/r22.claim: An oath is not accepted as proof here, since the hypocrites swore falsely.
JISHUMI:v1p835/r22.anchor: وتدل على أنه لا يعتبر القسم؛ لأنهم كانوا يحلفون كاذبين

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p278#2/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p278#2/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p278#2/r1.claim: His speech pleases you and looms large in your heart; something amazing is what seems great to the mind.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p278#2/r1.anchor: أي يروقك ويعظم في قلبك ومنه الشيء العجيب الذي يعظم في النفس

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p278#2/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p278#2/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p278#2/r2.claim: The man is al-Akhnas ibn Shariq, eloquent and smooth-tongued; he softened his speech to the Messenger, professed love and Islam, and claimed God knew he was truthful.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p278#2/r2.anchor: وهو الأخنس بن شريق كان رجلا حلو المنطق اذا لقي رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ألان له القول

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p278#2/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p278#2/r3.speaker: قيل
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p278#2/r3.claim: Alternatively, it applies generally to hypocrites, whose tongues are sweet while their hearts are bitter as colocynth.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p278#2/r3.anchor: وقيل هو عام في المنافقين كانت تحلولي ألسنتهم وقلوبهم امر من الصبر

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p278#2/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p278#2/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p278#2/r4.claim: “In the life of this world” may modify “his speech”: he professes love falsely for worldly gain, not for the hereafter or sincere faith.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p278#2/r4.anchor: قلت بالقول أي يعجبك ما يقوله في معنى الدنيا لأن ادعاءه المحبة بالباطل يطلب به حظا من حظوظ الدنيا

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p278#2/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p278#2/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p278#2/r5.claim: Alternatively, it modifies “pleases you”: his eloquence impresses in this life, but not at judgment when he stammers or is not permitted to speak.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p278#2/r5.anchor: ويجوز ان يتعلق بيعجبك أي قوله حلو فصيح في الدنيا فهو يعجبك ولا يعجبك في الآخرة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p278#3/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p278#3/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p278#3/r1.claim: He swears that God witnesses the love and Islam he says are in his heart.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p278#3/r1.anchor: أي يحلف ويقول الله شاهد على ما في قلبي من محبتك ومن الإسلام

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p278#3/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p278#3/r2.speaker: أبي
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p278#3/r2.claim: Ubayy’s codex reads “and he calls God as witness.”

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p278#3/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p278#3/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p278#3/r3.claim: He is fierce in argument and hostile to Muslims.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p278#3/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p278#3/r4.speaker: قيل
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p278#3/r4.claim: It is said that he feuded with Thaqif, raided them at night, destroyed livestock, and burned crops.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p278#3/r4.anchor: وقيل كان بينه وبين ثقيف خصومة فبيتهم ليلا وأهلك مواشيهم واحرق زروعهم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p278#3/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p278#3/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p278#3/r5.claim: The genitive can mean “most contentious in dispute,” or al-khiṣām can be a plural of opponent, making him the fiercest of opponents.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p278#3/r5.anchor: وإضافة الألد بمعنى في كقولهم ثبت الغدر أو جعل الخصام ألد على المبالغة

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p264/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p264/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p264/r1.claim: One interpretation is that his speech in worldly life is beautiful and good.

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p264/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p264/r2.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p264/r2.claim: The alternative is that he professes love for the Messenger and eagerness for his religion.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p264/r2.anchor: والثاني : من حب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم , والرغبة في دينه .

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p264/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p264/r3.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p264/r3.claim: One view is that he says God should witness his claim while his inner state contradicts it.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p264/r3.anchor: أحدها : أن يقول : اللهم اشهد علي فيه , وضميره بخلافه .

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p264/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p264/r4.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p264/r4.claim: Another says his heart contains what God witnesses to be contrary to his claim.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p264/r4.anchor: والثاني : معناه : وفي قلبه ما يشهد الله أنه بخلافه .

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p264/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p264/r5.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p264/r5.claim: A third view says he invokes God to attest to his heart's truth while knowing his claim is false.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p264/r5.anchor: والثالث : معناه : ويستشهد الله على صحة ما في قلبه , ويعلم أنه بخلافه .

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p264/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p264/r6.speaker: ابن مسعود
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p264/r6.claim: Ibn Masud's reading has yastashhidu, 'he calls God to witness,' instead of yushhidu.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p264/r6.anchor: وهي في قراءة ابن مسعود { ويستشهد الله على ما في قلبه } .

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p264/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p264/r7.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p264/r7.claim: Aladd describes a man who is fiercely contentious.

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p264/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p264/r8.speaker: الخليل
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p264/r8.claim: Al-Khalil analyzes khisam as a verbal noun.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p264/r8.anchor: أحدهما : أنه مصدر , وهو قول الخليل .

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p264/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p264/r9.speaker: الزجاج
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p264/r9.claim: Al-Zajjaj analyzes khisam as the plural of khasim, an opponent.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p264/r9.anchor: والثاني : أنه جمع خصيم , وهو قول الزجاج .

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p264/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p264/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p264/r10.claim: Ibn Abbas explains it as meaning a person given to argument.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p264/r10.anchor: أحدها : أنه ذو جدال , وهو قول ابن عباس .

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p264/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p264/r11.speaker: مجاهد، السدي
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p264/r11.claim: Mujahid and al-Suddi say he twists an argument instead of disputing fairly.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p264/r11.anchor: والثاني : يعني أنه غير مستقيم الخصومة , لكنه معوجها , وهذا قول مجاهد , والسدي .

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p264/r12.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p264/r12.speaker: الحسن البصري
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p264/r12.claim: Hasan al-Basri says he is a liar.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p264/r12.anchor: والثالث : يعني أنه كاذب , في قول الحسن البصري .

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p264/r13.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p264/r13.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p264/r13.claim: Qatada says he is fiercely hard-hearted in disobeying God.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p264/r13.anchor: والرابع : أنه شديد القسوة في معصية الله , وهو قول قتادة .

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p264/r14.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p264/r14.speaker: النبي
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p264/r14.claim: Through Ibn Abi Mulayka, Aisha reports the Prophet saying that the most hated men to God are the contentious disputant.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p264/r14.anchor: وقد روى ابن أبي مليكة , عن عائشة , أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال : ( أبغض الرجال إلى الله تعالى الألد الخصم )

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p264/r15.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p264/r15.speaker: ابن عباس، الحسن
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p264/r15.claim: Ibn Abbas and Hasan say the person described here and in the following verses is a hypocrite.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p264/r15.anchor: أحدهما : أنه صفة للمنافق , وهذا قول ابن عباس , والحسن .

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p264/r16.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p264/r16.speaker: السدي
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p264/r16.claim: Al-Suddi says these verses were revealed about al-Akhnas ibn Shariq.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p264/r16.anchor: والثاني : أنها نزلت في الأخنس بن شريق , وهو قول السدي .

MUQATIL:2:204-206/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:2:204-206/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:2:204-206/r1.claim: The passage concerns al-Akhnas ibn Shariq, who professed love for Muhammad and swore he would follow Islam; the Prophet welcomed him though his inward intent differed.
MUQATIL:2:204-206/r1.anchor: نزلت فى الأخنس بن شريق بن عمرو بن وهب بن أبى سلمة الثقفى

MUQATIL:2:204-206/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:2:204-206/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:2:204-206/r2.claim: His appeal to God refers to his oath; he claimed that his words were true in his heart.

MUQATIL:2:204-206/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:2:204-206/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:2:204-206/r3.claim: Aldd al-khiṣām means arguing falsely; 19:97 likewise describes people as fiercely disputatious.
MUQATIL:2:204-206/r3.anchor:
كقوله سبحانه:
وتنذر به قوما لدا

MUQATIL:2:204-206/r9.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:2:204-206/r9.speaker: author
MUQATIL:2:204-206/r9.claim: Al-Akhnas was also called Ubayy ibn Shariq; he earned the name by turning back 300 Banu Zuhra men from Badr, arguing Muhammad was their nephew and should be spared whether truthful or false.
MUQATIL:2:204-206/r9.anchor: وكان الأخنس يسمى أبى بن شريق، من بني زهرة بن كعب

NASAFI-FULL:v1p99#2/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p99#2/r1.speaker: الأخنس بن شريق
NASAFI-FULL:v1p99#2/r1.claim: The verse was revealed about al-Akhnas ibn Sharīq: he spoke sweetly to the Messenger, professed love and Islam, and claimed God knew he was sincere.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p99#2/r1.anchor: كان الأخنس بن شريق حلو المنطق إذا لقى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ألان له القول وادعى أنه يحبه

NASAFI-FULL:v1p99#2/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p99#2/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p99#2/r2.claim: His speech pleases and impresses; the root sense is something marvelous that looms large in the mind.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p99#2/r2.anchor: يروقك ويعظم فى قلبك ومنه الشئ العجيب الذى يعظم فى النفس

NASAFI-FULL:v1p99#2/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p99#2/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p99#2/r3.claim: The phrase may modify ‘his speech’: he seeks worldly advantage through professed love, not the afterlife; or it may modify ‘pleases you’: his eloquence charms in this life but fails him in the next.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p99#2/r3.anchor: فى يتعلق بالقول أى يعجبك ما يقوله فى معنى الدنيا لأنه يطلب بادعاء المحبة حظ الدنيا

NASAFI-FULL:v1p99#2/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p99#2/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p99#2/r4.claim: He swears, saying that God witnesses the love and Islam in his heart.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p99#2/r4.anchor: أى يحلف ويقول الله شاهد على ما في قلبي من محبتك ومن الإسلام

NASAFI-FULL:v1p99#2/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p99#2/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p99#2/r5.claim: Aladd means intensely contentious and hostile to Muslims; al-khiṣām may be a verbal noun (‘in disputation’) or a plural of khaṣm, ‘opponent.’
NASAFI-FULL:v1p99#2/r5.anchor: شديد الجدال والعداوة للمسلمين والخصام المخاصمة والإضافة بمعنى فى

NASAFI-FULL:v1p99#2/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p99#2/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p99#2/r6.claim: If khiṣām is a verbal noun, the construction means ‘most contentious in disputation’; if it is the plural of khaṣm, it means ‘the fiercest of opponents in contention.’
NASAFI-FULL:v1p99#2/r6.anchor: فتقديره ألد فى الخصومة أو الخصام جمع خصم كصعب وصعاب والتقدير وهو أشد الخصوم خصومة

BURSEVI:v1p264#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p264#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p264#2/r2.claim: To be impressed is to find something pleasing, incline toward it, and esteem it; al-Rāghib describes wonder as perplexity at not knowing a thing's cause.
BURSEVI:v1p264#2/r2.anchor: قال الراغب التعجب حيرة تعرض للإنسان عند الجهل بسبب الشيء

BURSEVI:v1p264#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p264#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p264#2/r3.claim: One reading links the phrase to the speech: the person pleases you by what he says about worldly life, seeking worldly advantage rather than the Hereafter.
BURSEVI:v1p264#2/r3.anchor: متعلق بالقول أي : يسرك ما يقوله في معنى الدنيا وحقها

BURSEVI:v1p264#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p264#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p264#2/r4.claim: Alternatively, his eloquence and sweetness impress people in this world, but his falsehood and ugliness will become apparent in the Hereafter.
BURSEVI:v1p264#2/r4.anchor: أو يعجبك قوله في الدنيا بحلاوته وفصاحته لا في الآخرة

BURSEVI:v1p264#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p264#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p264#2/r5.claim: He says that God witnesses the love and Islam in his heart to agree with what his tongue professes.
BURSEVI:v1p264#2/r5.anchor: يقول الله شاهد أن ما في قلبي من المحبة والإسلام

BURSEVI:v1p264#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p264#2/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p264#2/r6.claim: He is the most intense adversary in hostility and disputes against Muslims; لدد means severity in disputation, and خصام is a verbal noun like قتال and جدال, with ألد added in the sense of 'in'.

BURSEVI:v1p264#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p264#2/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p264#2/r7.claim: The verse was revealed about al-Akh nas ibn Shurayq al-Thaqafī, handsome and eloquent, who professed alliance, Islam, love, and sincerity toward the Prophet.
BURSEVI:v1p264#2/r7.anchor: نزلت في الأخنس بن شريف الثقفي

BURSEVI:v1p264#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p264#2/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p264#2/r8.claim: Claiming love and sincerity without matching heart and tongue is the conduct of heretics and hypocrites; a lover acts only as the beloved loves.
BURSEVI:v1p264#2/r8.anchor: والمحب لا يفعل إلا ما يحب محبوبه

BURSEVI:v1p264#2/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p264#2/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p264#2/r9.claim: Arabic verse and a couplet by Ḥāfiẓ illustrate that professed love is contradicted by disobedient deeds and falsehood; the true lover obeys the beloved.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:204/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:204/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:204/r1.claim: After contrasting those who ask only for worldly good in 2:200 with believers asking for both abodes in 2:201, the passage turns to hypocrites who profess faith but conceal unbelief.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:204/r1.anchor: لما ذكر الذين قصرت همتهم على الدنيا في قوله:

QURTUBI-FULL:2:204/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:204/r2.speaker: السدي
QURTUBI-FULL:2:204/r2.claim: Al-Suddi and other exegetes say the verse concerns al-Akhnas ibn Shurayq, who withdrew at Badr with 300 allies, later professed Islam to the Prophet, then burned Muslims' crops and killed their donkeys.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:204/r2.anchor: قال السدي وغيره من المفسرين: نزلت في الأخنس بن شريق، واسمه أبي، والأخنس لقب لقب به لأنه خنس يوم بدر

QURTUBI-FULL:2:204/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:204/r3.speaker: المهدوي
QURTUBI-FULL:2:204/r3.claim: Al-Mahdawi says the al-Akhnas account also occasioned 68:10–11 and 104:1.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:204/r3.anchor: قال المهدوي: وفيه نزلت ولا تطع كل حلاف مهين هماز مشآء بنميم

QURTUBI-FULL:2:204/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:204/r4.speaker: ابن عطية
QURTUBI-FULL:2:204/r4.claim: Ibn Atiyya says it has never been established that al-Akhnas became Muslim.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:204/r4.anchor: قال ابن عطية: ما ثبت قط أن الأخنس أسلم.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:204/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:204/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:2:204/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas says the verse concerned hypocrites who disparaged those killed at al-Rajiʿ, including Asim ibn Thabit and Khubayb, mocking them for neither staying home nor fulfilling their companion's mission.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:204/r5.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: نزلت في قوم من المنافقين تكلموا في الذين قتلوا في غزوة الرجيع: عاصم بن ثابت، وخبيب

QURTUBI-FULL:2:204/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:204/r6.speaker: قتادة ومجاهد وجماعة من العلماء
QURTUBI-FULL:2:204/r6.claim: Qatada, Mujahid, and others take the verse generally of anyone concealing unbelief, hypocrisy, lies, or harm while speaking otherwise; the next verse then describes the martyrs of al-Rajiʿ.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:204/r6.anchor: وقال قتادة ومجاهد وجماعة من العلماء: نزلت في كل مبطن كفرا أو نفاقا

QURTUBI-FULL:2:204/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:204/r7.speaker: الترمذي
QURTUBI-FULL:2:204/r7.claim: A report in al-Tirmidhi cites a divine scripture describing servants with honey-sweet tongues and bitter hearts who trade religion for worldly gain, then warns of a trial that will bewilder the patient.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:204/r7.anchor: وهي تشبه ما ورد في الترمذي أن في بعض كتب الله تعالى: إن من عباد الله قوما ألسنتهم أحلى من العسل

QURTUBI-FULL:2:204/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:204/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:204/r8.claim: To call God to witness means he claims that God knows he is speaking truthfully.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:204/r8.anchor: ومعنى «ويشهد الله» أي يقول: الله يعلم أني أقول حقا.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:204/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:204/r9.speaker: ابن محيصن
QURTUBI-FULL:2:204/r9.claim: Ibn Muhaysin reads the verb actively and Allah in the nominative: the speech pleases, while God knows the speaker's heart contradicts it; 63:1 supports this sense.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:204/r9.anchor: وقرأ ابن محيصن «ويشهد الله على ما فى قلبه» بفتح الياء والهاء في «يشهد» «الله» بالرفع

QURTUBI-FULL:2:204#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:204#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:2:204#2/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas reads, God bears witness to what is in his heart.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:204#2/r1.anchor: وقراءة ابن عباس { والله يشهدعلى ما فى قلبه }.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:204#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:204#2/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:204#2/r2.claim: Al-Qurtubi says the majority reading is more emphatic in blame: the speaker deliberately commits to gracious words, then reveals their opposite inwardly.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:204#2/r2.anchor: وقراءة الجماعة أبلغ في الذم لأنه قوى على نفسه التزام الكلام الحسن، ثم ظهر من باطنه خلافه.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:204#2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:204#2/r3.speaker: أبي وابن مسعود
QURTUBI-FULL:2:204#2/r3.claim: Ubayy and Ibn Masud read the causative form meaning he calls God to witness what is in his heart; al-Qurtubi says it supports the majority reading.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:204#2/r3.anchor: وقرأ أبي وابن مسعود «ويستشهد الله على ما في قلبه» وهي حجة لقراءة الجماعة.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:204#2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:204#2/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:204#2/r4.claim: The verse advises caution in religious and worldly affairs and scrutiny of witnesses and judges; rulers should investigate rather than rely solely on professions of faith and apparent virtue.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:204#2/r4.anchor: وفي هذه الآية دليل وتنبيه على الاحتياط فيما يتعلق بأمور الدين والدنيا، واستبراء أحوال الشهود والقضاة

QURTUBI-FULL:2:204#2/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:204#2/r5.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:2:204#2/r5.claim: The objection cites the Prophet's statement that he was commanded to fight people until they profess God's oneness, and his instruction to judge according to what he hears.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:204#2/r5.anchor: فإن قيل: هذا يعارضه قوله عليه السلام: " أمرت أن أقاتل الناس حتى يقولوا لا إله إلا الله " الحديث، وقوله:

QURTUBI-FULL:2:204#2/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:204#2/r6.speaker: ابن العربي
QURTUBI-FULL:2:204#2/r6.claim: Ibn al-Arabi answers that those statements belonged to early Islam, when professing Islam guaranteed safety, whereas corruption later became widespread.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:204#2/r6.anchor: فالجواب أن هذا كان في صدر الإسلام، حيث كان إسلامهم سلامتهم، وأما وقد عم الفساد فلا قاله ابن العربي.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:204#2/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:204#2/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:204#2/r7.claim: Al-Qurtubi holds that people are judged by outward appearances until contrary evidence appears, citing Umar: revelation has ended, good apparent conduct merits trust, and hidden states are God's concern.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:204#2/r7.anchor: قلت: والصحيح أن الظاهر يعمل عليه حتى يتبين خلافه لقول عمر بن الخطاب رضي الله عنه في صحيح البخاري: أيها الناس، إن الوحي قد انقطع

QURTUBI-FULL:2:204#2/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:204#2/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:204#2/r8.claim: Al-ald means severe in disputation; it is the masculine form, with feminine ladāʾ and plural ahl al-ladad, and the root can describe prevailing in an argument.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:204#2/r8.anchor: الألد: الشديد الخصومة وهو رجل ألد، وامرأة لداء، وهم أهل لدد. وقد لددت بكسر الدال تلد بالفتح

QURTUBI-FULL:2:204#2/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:204#2/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:204#2/r9.claim: Al-Qurtubi derives al-ald from the two sides of the neck: whatever side a disputant takes, he wins.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:204#2/r9.anchor: والألد مشتق من اللديدين، وهما صفحتا العنق، أي في أي جانب أخذ من الخصومة غلب.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:204#2/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:204#2/r10.speaker: الخليل
QURTUBI-FULL:2:204#2/r10.claim: Al-Khalil analyzes al-khisām as the verbal noun of khāṣama.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:204#2/r10.anchor: و «الخصام» في الآية مصدر خاصم قاله الخليل.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:204#2/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:204#2/r11.speaker: الزجاج
QURTUBI-FULL:2:204#2/r11.claim: Al-Zajjaj instead analyzes al-khisām as a plural of khaṣm, like kalb/kilāb and ṣaʿb/ṣiʿāb.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:204#2/r11.anchor: وقيل: جمع خصم قاله الزجاج ككلب وكلاب، وصعب وصعاب، وضخم وضخام.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:204#2/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:204#2/r12.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:204#2/r12.claim: The phrase means the fiercest disputant: his words sound appealing when he argues, though his inward case is false.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:204#2/r12.anchor: والمعنى أشد المخاصمين خصومة، أي هو ذو جدال، إذا كلمك وراجعك رأيت لكلامه طلاوة وباطنه باطل.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:204#2/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:204#2/r13.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:204#2/r13.claim: The description shows that disputation is permissible only when what is outwardly said agrees with what is inwardly true.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:204#2/r13.anchor: وهذا يدل على أن الجدال لا يجوز إلا بما ظاهره وباطنه سواء.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:204#2/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:204#2/r14.speaker: الشاعر
QURTUBI-FULL:2:204#2/r14.claim: The first cited poem depicts an adversary whose enmity boils in his breast, illustrating the force of al-ald.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:204#2/r14.anchor: قال الشاعر: وألد ذى حنق علي كأنما

QURTUBI-FULL:2:204#2/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:204#2/r15.speaker: آخر
QURTUBI-FULL:2:204#2/r15.claim: A second poem calls someone beneath the earth a determined, obstinate opponent, providing another poetic example of al-ald.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:204#2/r15.anchor: وقال آخر: إن تحت التراب عزما وحزما

QURTUBI-FULL:2:204#3/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:204#3/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:2:204#3/r1.claim: Aisha reports the Prophet saying that the most hateful of men to God is the obstinate, contentious adversary.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:204#3/r1.anchor: " إن أبغض الرجال إلى الله الألد الخصم ".

RAZI-FULL:v5p167#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p167#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p167#2/r1.claim: After describing the unbeliever who asks only for worldly good and the Muslim who asks for good here and hereafter, the passage introduces the hypocrite’s traits.
RAZI-FULL:v5p167#2/r1.anchor: لما بين أن الذين يشهدون مشاعر الحج فريقان : كافر وهو الذي يقول

RAZI-FULL:v5p167#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p167#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p167#2/r2.claim: The descriptions encourage sound conduct in hearts and limbs and remind people that God cannot be kept unaware of their inner affairs.
RAZI-FULL:v5p167#2/r2.anchor: والغرض بكل ذلك أن يبعث العباد على الطريقة الحسنة فيما يتصل بأفعال القلوب والجوارح

RAZI-FULL:v5p167#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p167#2/r3.speaker: المفسرون
RAZI-FULL:v5p167#2/r3.claim: Exegetes differ: some restrict the passage to particular people, while others take it as general for anyone possessing its described traits.
RAZI-FULL:v5p167#2/r3.anchor: ثم اختلف المفسرون على قولين منهم من قال : هذه الآية مختصة بأقوام معينين ومنهم من قال : إنها عامة

RAZI-FULL:v5p167#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p167#2/r4.speaker: الرواية الأولى
RAZI-FULL:v5p167#2/r4.claim: One report identifies al-Akhnas ibn Shurayq, an ally of Banū Zuhra, who professed Islam, claimed love for the Prophet, then burned a Muslim’s crops and killed livestock.
RAZI-FULL:v5p167#2/r4.anchor: فالرواية الأولى : أنها نزلت في الأخنس بن شريق الثقفي ، وهو حليف لبني زهرة أقبل إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

RAZI-FULL:v5p167#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p167#2/r5.speaker: قال آخرون
RAZI-FULL:v5p167#2/r5.claim: Another account says al-Akhnas advised Banū Zuhra to withdraw from Badr, claiming they would benefit whether Muhammad was truthful or false; he withdrew with 300 men.
RAZI-FULL:v5p167#2/r5.anchor: وقال آخرون المراد بقوله تعالى : { يعجبك قوله } هو أن الأخنس أشار على بني زهرة بالرجوع يوم بدر

RAZI-FULL:v5p167#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p167#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p167#2/r6.claim: Al-Rāzī rejects the Badr-withdrawal identification as weak: it does not merit condemnation, whereas the verse is framed as censure; he prefers the first account.
RAZI-FULL:v5p167#2/r6.anchor: وعندي أن هذا القول ضعيف وذلك لأنه بهذا الفعل لا يستوجب الذم وقوله تعالى : { ومن الناس من يعجبك

RAZI-FULL:v5p168/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p168/r1.speaker: ابن عباس والضحاك
RAZI-FULL:v5p168/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and al-Ḍaḥḥāk report that Quraysh lured the Prophet into sending learned companions, then seventy riders killed and crucified them at al-Rajīʿ; the next verse recalls such martyrs.
RAZI-FULL:v5p168/r1.anchor: والرواية الثانية : في سبب نزول هذه الآية ما روي عن ابن عباس والضحاك أن كفار قريش

RAZI-FULL:v5p168/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p168/r2.speaker: أكثر المحققين من المفسرين
RAZI-FULL:v5p168/r2.claim: Al-Rāzī prefers the general reading favored by most careful exegetes: the verse covers everyone characterized by these traits, whether or not revelation began with a particular case.
RAZI-FULL:v5p168/r2.anchor: القول الثاني : في الآية وهو اختيار أكثر المحققين من المفسرين ، أن هذه الآية عامة في حق كل من كان

RAZI-FULL:v5p168/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p168/r3.speaker: محمد بن كعب القرظي
RAZI-FULL:v5p168/r3.claim: Muḥammad ibn Kaʿb al-Quraẓī says that even if the verse was revealed about a named person, it can still apply generally to all with those traits.
RAZI-FULL:v5p168/r3.anchor: ونقل عن محمد بن كعب القرظي ، أنه جرى بينه وبين غيره كلام في هذه الآية

RAZI-FULL:v5p168/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p168/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p168/r4.claim: The phrase “among people” can refer to one person or many; “God is witness” does not prove a singular referent because grammar may follow wording rather than meaning.
RAZI-FULL:v5p168/r4.anchor: أن قوله : { ومن الناس } إشارة إلى بعضهم ، فيحتمل الواحد ويحتمل الجمع ، وقوله : { ويشهد الله }

RAZI-FULL:v5p168/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p168/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p168/r5.claim: A judgment attached to a relevant description signals that the traits cause condemnation, so everyone possessing them deserves blame.
RAZI-FULL:v5p168/r5.anchor: أن ترتب الحكم على الوصف المناسب مشعر بالعلية ، فلما ذم الله تعالى قوما ووصفهم بصفات توجب

RAZI-FULL:v5p168/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p168/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p168/r6.claim: The general reading gives greater benefit by warning all morally responsible people away from the condemned path.
RAZI-FULL:v5p168/r6.anchor: أن الحمل على العموم أكثر فائدة ، وذلك لأنه يكون زجرا لكل المكلفين عن تلك الطريق المذمومة

RAZI-FULL:v5p168/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p168/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p168/r7.claim: Generality is the safer reading: it includes the reported individual, whereas restricting the verse to him would exclude everyone else.
RAZI-FULL:v5p168/r7.anchor: أن هذا أقرب إلى الاحتياط لأنا إذا حملنا الآية على العموم دخل فيه ذلك الشخص

RAZI-FULL:v5p168/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p168/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p168/r8.claim: The five traits do not prove hypocrisy: each can also characterize a show-off or another sinner; hypocrites are included, but not every person described must be one.
RAZI-FULL:v5p168/r8.anchor: فثبت أنا متى حملنا الآية على الموصوف بهذه الصفات الخمسة دخل فيها المنافق والمرائي

RAZI-FULL:v5p168/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p168/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p168/r9.claim: Being pleasing in worldly speech carries only an implication of blame, since the phrase suggests smooth talk about worldly matters.
RAZI-FULL:v5p168/r9.anchor: لأن الإنسان إذا قيل : إنه حلو الكلام فيما يتعلق بالدنيا أوهم نوعا من المذمة

RAZI-FULL:v5p168/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p168/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p168/r10.claim: Calling God witness does not establish hypocrisy: the verse never says he professes Islam while inwardly rejecting it; he may instead hide corruption and display its opposite as a show-off.
RAZI-FULL:v5p168/r10.anchor: فإن أضمرنا فيه أن يشهد الله على ما في قلبه مع أن قلبه بخلاف ذلك فالكلام

RAZI-FULL:v5p168/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p168/r11.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p168/r11.claim: Being fiercely argumentative does not by itself entail hypocrisy.
RAZI-FULL:v5p168/r11.anchor: وثالثها : قوله : { وهو ألد الخصام } وهذا أيضا لا يوجب النفاق

RAZI-FULL:v5p169/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p169/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p169/r1.claim: يعجبك means his speech pleases you and grows large in your estimation, like something wondrous that looms in the mind.
RAZI-FULL:v5p169/r1.anchor: والمعنى : يروقك ويعظم في قلبك ومنه الشيء العجيب الذي يعظم في النفس

RAZI-FULL:v5p169/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p169/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p169/r2.claim: One reading takes the phrase as speech that impresses when he seeks worldly interests, like admiring someone’s words on a particular matter.
RAZI-FULL:v5p169/r2.anchor: أنه نظير قول القائل : يعجبني كلام فلان في هذه المسألة والمعنى : يعجبك قوله وكلامه عندما يتكلم

RAZI-FULL:v5p169/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p169/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p169/r3.claim: A second reading contrasts this life with the afterlife: he is eloquent and sweet-tongued here, but fear of God’s majesty leaves him stammering there.
RAZI-FULL:v5p169/r3.anchor: أن يكون التقدير : يعجبك قوله وكلامه في الحياة الدنيا وإن كان لا يعجبك قوله وكلامه في الآخرة

RAZI-FULL:v5p169/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p169/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p169/r4.claim: He backs up his truth-claim by calling God as witness; this can be a sworn oath or a statement that God witnesses the claim, without an oath.
RAZI-FULL:v5p169/r4.anchor: فالمعنى أنه يقرر صدقه في كلامه ودعواه

RAZI-FULL:v5p169/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p169/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p169/r5.claim: Al-Rāzī notes that most readers pronounce يشهد with ḍamma on yāʾ, meaning the speaker calls God to witness what is in his heart.
RAZI-FULL:v5p169/r5.anchor: بضم الياء ، أي هذا القائل يشهد الله على ما في ضميره

RAZI-FULL:v5p169/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p169/r6.speaker: ابن محيصن
RAZI-FULL:v5p169/r6.claim: Ibn Muḥayṣin reads يشهد with fatḥa on yāʾ: God knows that the speaker’s heart contradicts what he displays.
RAZI-FULL:v5p169/r6.anchor: وقرأ ابن محيصن { يشهد * الله على ما فى قلبه } بفتح الياء

RAZI-FULL:v5p169/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p169/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p169/r7.claim: The first reading is more blameworthy: it portrays pretentious false attestation about hypocrisy and ostentation; the second establishes only that he is lying, not that he falsely swears by God.
RAZI-FULL:v5p169/r7.anchor: فالقراءة الأولى : تدل على كونه مرائيا وعلى أنه يشهد الله باطلا على نفاقه وريائه

RAZI-FULL:v5p169/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p169/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p169/r8.claim: الألد means severe in disputation; the verse’s phrase parallels “a contentious people” and “a people given to dispute.”
RAZI-FULL:v5p169/r8.anchor: الألد : الشديد الخصومة ، يقال : رجل ألد ، وقوم لد ، وقال الله تعالى : { وتنذر به قوما لدا }

RAZI-FULL:v5p169/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p169/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p169/r9.claim: The singular is ألد and plural لُدّ; the present of لَدَّ is pronounced with an open lām, while لَدَدْتُ الرجل أَلُدُّه means I defeated him in argument.
RAZI-FULL:v5p169/r9.anchor: يقال : منه لد يلد ، بفتح اللام

RAZI-FULL:v5p169/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p169/r10.speaker: الزجاج
RAZI-FULL:v5p169/r10.claim: Al-Zajjāj derives the word from the two sides of the neck or valley: whatever side or argumentative route an opponent takes, this disputant overcomes him.
RAZI-FULL:v5p169/r10.anchor: قال الزجاج اشتقاقه من لديدتي العنق وهما صفحتاه ، ولديدي الوادي ، وهما جانباه

RAZI-FULL:v5p170/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p170/r1.speaker: خليل
RAZI-FULL:v5p170/r1.claim: Khalil reads al-khiṣām as a verbal noun meaning disputation, comparable to qitāl and ṭaʿām.
RAZI-FULL:v5p170/r1.anchor: قول خليل : إنه مصدر بمعنى المخاصمة

RAZI-FULL:v5p170/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p170/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p170/r2.claim: One construction treats the genitive as if introduced by fī: he is most contentious in disputation.
RAZI-FULL:v5p170/r2.anchor: أحدهما : أنه بمعنى { فى } والتقدير : ألد في الخصام

RAZI-FULL:v5p170/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p170/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p170/r3.claim: Alternatively, the dispute itself is called most contentious as an intensifying expression.
RAZI-FULL:v5p170/r3.anchor: أنه جعل الخصام ألد على سبيل المبالغة

RAZI-FULL:v5p170/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p170/r4.speaker: الزجاج
RAZI-FULL:v5p170/r4.claim: Al-Zajjāj takes al-khiṣām as a plural of خصم, so the phrase means the most disputatious of opponents.
RAZI-FULL:v5p170/r4.anchor: أشد الخصوم خصومة ، وهذا قول الزجاج

RAZI-FULL:v5p170/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p170/r5.speaker: المفسرون
RAZI-FULL:v5p170/r5.claim: Exegetes say the verse was revealed about al-Akhnas ibn Shurayq, and also connect him with verses in al-Humaza and al-Qalam.
RAZI-FULL:v5p170/r5.anchor: قال المفسرون : هذه الآية نزلت في الأخنس بن شريق

RAZI-FULL:v5p170/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p170/r6.speaker: مجاهد
RAZI-FULL:v5p170/r6.claim: Mujāhid explains the phrase as a petitioner who does not act uprightly.
RAZI-FULL:v5p170/r6.anchor: قال مجاهد { ألد الخصام } معناه : طالب لا يستقيم

RAZI-FULL:v5p170/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p170/r7.speaker: السدي
RAZI-FULL:v5p170/r7.claim: Al-Suddī glosses the phrase as crooked in disputation.

RAZI-FULL:v5p170/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p170/r8.speaker: قتادة
RAZI-FULL:v5p170/r8.claim: Qatāda says he argues falsely, is harsh in disobeying God, eloquent in speech, yet ignorant in action.

RAZI-FULL:v5p170/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p170/r9.speaker: المنكرون للنظر والجدل
RAZI-FULL:v5p170/r9.claim: Opponents of rational inquiry cite the verse to argue that intense disputation is blameworthy, or reason would not be condemned.
RAZI-FULL:v5p170/r9.anchor: تمسك المنكرون للنظر والجدل بهذه الآية

RAZI-FULL:v5p170/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p170/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p170/r10.claim: Rāzī answers this objection by referring back to his discussion of the prohibition on disputation during pilgrimage.
RAZI-FULL:v5p170/r10.anchor: وجوابه ما تقدم في قوله : { ولا جدال في الحج }
